δακτυλόδεικτος.definition: pointed at with the finger, A.Ag.1332 , cf. PLond.ined.1821

δακτυλόδικτος.definition: thrown from the fingers, of the humming of a top, A.Fr.57 codd. Str

δακτυλοειδής.definition: like a finger, Philem. Gloss. ap. Ath.11.468f, Ruf.Oss.22

δακτυλοκαμψόδυνος.definition: wearying the fingers by keeping them bent, APl.1.18

δαμαλίζω.definition: poet. = to subdue, Pi.P.5.121 codd.:—Med., E.Hipp.231

δαμασίμβροτος.definition: taming mortals, man-slaying, Simon.218; Pi.O.9.79; B.12.50

δαμασίφως.definition: = Simon.232; of Ares, prob. in Tim.Pers.22

δανείζω.definition: fut. D.35.52: aor; Med., have lent to one, borrow, Ar.Nu.1306, etc.; Lys.17.2; D.1.15; 34.23:—Act. and Med. opposed, ap.D.35.11:—Pass., of the money, to be lent out, Ar.Nu.756, X.HG2.4.28, D.33.12

δάνειον.definition: loan, D.34.12; Arist.EN1164b32: pl., Men.Mon.97; POxy.1262.16 : —written LXXDe.15.8,al

δανεισμός.definition: money-lending, IG22.1172, Pl.Lg.842d; borrowing, Pl.R.573e , POxy.799 , Plu.2.706b: metaph., E.El.858

δανειστής.definition: money-lender or creditor; borrower, IG12.67.41,68.4 , Plu.Sol.13

δαπανάω.definition: —Pass., pres. part. (as if from; consume, use up, Arist.GA757a25; Onos.1.5:—Pass., Arist.GA745a13; of time, App.Pun.130; destroy, consume, Ph.2.208; App.BC1.94; of persons, to be destroyed, Ph.2.43; ib.433; App.BC5.79…

δαπάνημα.definition: cost, expense, mostly in pl., X.Cyr.8.1.9, Philem.96.6, IG7.2712.32 ; BGU1130.21 , etc.; want of necessaries, Plb.9.42.4: sg. in Arist.EN1122a24, CIG3600 , etc

δάπανος.definition: = Th.5.103; cj. in Longin.44.11: c. gen., Plu.2.624d

δαρθάνω.definition: sleep, Hierocl.in CA19 p.461 M.: aor. 2 Od.20.143

δασμολογέω.definition: fut. Isoc.Ep.7.4:—collect as tribute; c.acc. pers., subject one to tribute, Isoc.4.132; Hyp.Eux.36:—Pass., Isoc.4.123

δασμοφορέω.definition: to be subject to tribute, A.Pers.586 :—Pass., tribute is paid one, X.Cyr.8.6.4

δασυγένειος.definition: with thick beard, v.l. for Tz.ad Lyc.307

δασύθριξ.definition: gen. hairy, AP6.113 , Nonn.D.48.673; AP9.136 ; of a person, ib.11.345, cf. Polem. Phgn.5

δασύστερνος.definition: shaggy-breasted, Hes.Op.514; of Nessus, S.Tr.557; of a Satyr, Nonn.D.28.90

δατύσσω.definition: devour, Hsch.; swallow, dub. l.in Aret.SD2.13

δαφνέλαιον.definition: oil of bay, Dsc.1.40 tit. , Sch.Nic.Al.198

δαφνηφορέω.definition: bear boughs or crowns of bay, Paus.9.10.4, Plu.Aem.34, IG14.1293B, Hdn.2.2.10; of the Roman fasces laureati, Id.7.6.2; to be read for in D.C.37.21

δαφνηφορία.definition: bay-bearing, Boeotian festival in honour of Apollo, Procl. ap. Phot.Bibl.p.321 B

δαφνηφόρος.definition: bay-bearing, A.Supp.706; Subst., bearer of bays, at Eleusis, IG22.1092B25

δάφνιος.definition: f.l. for foreg., Hp.Morb.2.13; epith. of Artemis, Str.8.3.12

δαφνοειδής.definition: like bay, Thphr.HP9.15.5; spurge-laurel, Daphne Laureola, Hp.Nat.Mul.33, Dsc.4.146

δαφνοπώλης.definition: bay-seller, Com. epith. of Apollo, Ar.Fr.764

δαφνών.definition: laurel grove, Str.16.4.14 , Petron.126, Gell.2.20.9 , Peripl.M.Rubr.11

δαψίλεια.definition: abundance, plenty, Arist.HA572a3; Id.GA782b18; Plb.2.15.4; D.S.5.13, cf. Agatharch.95; Onos.35.2: metaph., Metrod.31

δαψιλεύομαι.definition: abound, Ph.Byz.Mir.3.2; to be anxious, careworn, LXX1 Ki.10.2

δέησις.definition: written petition, CPHerm.6.10, J.BJ7.5.2, Ph.2.586, PGen.16.10

δειγματισμός.definition: public inspection, verification; putting to shame, exposure, in pl., Vett.Val.43.26, Heph.Astr.2.32,34, PRyl.1.28.70

δειγματοάρτης.definition: inspector of the market, POxy.63.8 , PLond.3.1159.39

δειγματοκαταγωγός.definition: official who delivered samples of corn, PStrassb.31.6

δειλαίνω.definition: to be a coward or cowardly, Arist.EN1107a18, 1137a22, Plot.1.4.15:—Med., Luc.Ocyp.153, Pteb.58.27:—Pass., Hsch.; Id

δειλακρίων.definition: pitiable creature; in Com., poor fellow! Ar.Pax193, Av.143

δειλανδρέω.definition: to be cowardly, LXX2 Ma.8.13, 4 Ma.10.14

δειλιάω.definition: to be afraid, LXXDe.1.28, al., D.S.20.78, Paul.Aeg.3.76

δειλόομαι.definition: Pass., to be afraid, read by Nicanor in S.Ichn.150, cf. LXX1 Ma.16.6, D.S.20.78

δειμαλέος.definition: timid, Arist.Phgn.810a23; horrible, fearful, Batr.287, cj. in Thgn.1128

δειματίας.definition: epith. of Zeus, the Scarer, D.H.6.90

δειματόω.definition: frighten, Hdt.6.3, Ar.Ra.144, Ph.2.204:—Pass., A.Ch.845, S.Ichn.142, E.Andr.42, Pl.Ax.370a, etc

δεινάζω.definition: to be in straits, LXX2 Ma.4.35

δεινολογέομαι.definition: complain loudly, . . Hdt.1.44; . . Plu.Sert.6: abs., Hdt.4.68, Eus.Mynd.59

δεινοπάθεια.definition: exaggerated complaint, condemned by Poll.6.201, cf. Suid.s.v

δεινοπαθέω.definition: complain loudly of sufferings, D.40.53, Telesp.58H., Plb.12.16.9, Luc.Syr.D.24; D.S.19.75, Plu.2.781a

δεινοπροσωπέω.definition: to be stern of countenance, Arg.E.Ph

δείπνηστος.definition: meal-time, Od.17.170; Nic.Th.761 . = meal-time, = meal, Eust.1814.36.)

δειπνοκλήτωρ.definition: one who invites to dinner, v.l; = Artem. ap. Ath.4.171b:—hence Eust.766.58

δειπνοκρίτης.definition: judge of the feasts, of a religious official, Epigr. in CRAcad.Inscr.1907.141

δειπνοπίθηκος.definition: Com. name for a parasite, Com.Adesp.321

δειπνοποιέω.definition: prepare a dinner, X.Cyr.5.2.6 , Alciphr.2.1:— Med., dine, Th.4.103, Plu.2.225d

δειπνοφόρος.definition: carrying meals, of birds; carrying meat-offerings, Lys.Fr.311S., Hyp.Fr.88, Plu.Thes.23, IG3.371

δεισιδαιμονέω.definition: have superstitious fears, Plb.9.19.1, D.S.12.59, Polystr.9, etc.: rare in good sense, to be religious, Zaleuc. ap. Stob.4.2.19

δεισιδαιμονία.definition: fear of the gods, religious; in bad sense, superstition, Thphr.Char.16, Plb.12.24.5; D.S.1.83; title of work by Plu

δεισιδαίμων.definition: gen. fearing the gods; in good sense, pious, religious, X.Cyr.3.3.58, Ages.11.8; Arist.Pol.1315a1; IG14.1683: Comp. Act.Ap.17.22

δεκάβοιος.definition: worth ten oxen, a coin attributed to Theseus, Plu.Thes.25; from a law of Draco, Poll.2.61

δεκαδάκτυλος.definition: ten fingers long or broad; ten-fingered, D.C.47.40

δεκαδάρχης.definition: later form for = Lat; with or without name of an order of divine beings, Herm.in Phdr.p.134A., Dam.Pr.351

δεκαδαρχία.definition: government of ten, v.l. in Isoc.4.110; decuria of cavalry, Arr.Tact.42.1

δεκαδεύς.definition: one of a decury, X.Cyr.2.2.30; chairman of a board of ten, in acc. sg. IG4.748.21

δεκαέτηρος.definition: ten-yearly: a space of ten years. Pl.Lg.772b codd.:— fem. D.C.57.24: more freq. as Subst., period of ten years, prob. in Pl.l.c., Vett. Val.252.9, OGI722 :— also title of Orphic work, Suid

δεκαετής.definition: or ten years old; of or lasting ten years, Th.5.25,26 codd., Jul.Or.2.74b. — The statements of Gramm. as to the accentuation of this and similar words are confused, cf.Poll.1.54, EM765.21, Choerob.in Theod.1.167, 2.38…

δεκαετία.definition: space of ten years, Arist.Ath.3.1, cf. D.H.1.71, Str.15.1.43, Ph.1.531, Plu.Num.10

δεκάλιτρος.definition: weighing or worth ten Epich.10, Arist.Fr.510: as Subst., coin worth ten Sophr.37, cf. Poll.9.81

δεκάμηνος.definition: ten months old, X.Cyn.7.6, cf; in the tenth month, Hdt.9.3; Hp.Septim.7; prob. l. in Men.413; Arist.GA777b14: neut. pl. as Adv., ib.772b9

δεκαμναῖος.definition: or = sq., Plb.13.2.3; throwing a projectile weighing ten minae, Ph.Bel.51.49

δεκαμοιρία.definition: space of ten degrees of the zodiac, J.AJ3.7.7, Ptol.Alm.2.7, Anon. ap. Lyd.Ost.p.174 W.:— hence Adj. Heph.Astr.1.1

δεκάμοιρον.definition: name of an ointment, Orib. ap. Aët.12.62: perh. f.l. for a similar remedy, Alex.Trall.7.8

δεκαολυμπιονίκης.definition: winner of ten victories at Olympia, Sammelb.5225

δεκαπλάσιος.definition: tenfold, Hp.VM16 ; Pl.R.615b: c. gen., ten times greater than, Plb.21.22.15; mulct in ten times the amount, Lex ap.D.24.105 ; rob the state of a tenfold penalty, D.24.82. Adv. Hp.VM6

δεκαπλόος.definition: contr. = D.24.83; Arist.Ath.54.2, cf. Hyp.Dem.Fr.7: also in fem. IG5.1421.13

δεκάπολις.definition: district with ten cities, Decapolis, Ev.Matt.4.25, J.BJ3.9.7, IGRom.3.1057

δεκαπρωτεύω.definition: serve as member of JHS37.108 , CIG2929 , etc

δεκάρχης.definition: = decurion, Hdt.7.81; =; = Lat. decemvir, f.l. in D.H.2.14

δεκάσπορος χρόνος.definition: lapse of ten seed-times, i.e. ten years, E.Tr.20, cf. El.1154

δεκασταδιαῖος.definition: ten stadia high, Theo Sm.p.125 H.,al

δεκαστάδιον.definition: race-course of ten stadia, IG4.951.79 , HerzogKoische Forschungenp.55

δεκαστάτηρος.definition: in receipt of ten staters, Arr.An.7.23.3: Subst. sum of ten staters, Leg.Gort.9.49, Schwyzer 179a5 ; weight of ten staters, IG12.918

δεκατάλαντος.definition: weighing or worth ten talents, Ar.Fr.276; an action in which the damages were laid at ten talents, Aeschin.2.99

δεκατάρχης.definition: = Lat. decurio, in the Roman fleet, IG5.818.5 , Supp.Epigr.1.345

δεκάταρχος.definition: head of a PSI 4.337.4 ; PPetr.2p.6; v.l. for LXX1 Ma.3.55

δεκατευτήριον.definition: office for collection of custom-house, X.HG1.1.22

δεκατηφόρος.definition: tithe-paying, Call.Del.278; receiving tithe, epith. of Apollo at Megara, Paus.1.42.5: Dor. GDI5045 , etc

δεκτέος.definition: to be received, Luc.Herm.74; one must take or understand, Str.10.2.22, Sch.Th.Oxy. 853 vii 9

δεκτήρ.definition: title of an official receiver, IG5.274 , cf. Hsch., Suid

δέλεαρ.definition: Ep. ; Ep. gen. Numen. ap. Ath.7.305a; dat. pl. Opp.H.3.437: contr. in dat. Hsch.; neut. pl. cj. in Theoc.21.10:-bait, X.Mem.2.1.4, Plb.15.21.6 : metaph., bait for a person, E.Andr.264, cf. Fr.981.5, Luc.Rh.Pr.25 , etc…

δέλετρον.definition: = Numen. ap. Ath.7.287c, 306c; torch, Timach. ap. Ath.15.699e, Hsch

δελτογράφος.definition: writing on a tablet, recording, A.Eu.275

δελτοειδής.definition: delta-shaped, triangular, Hsch. s.v. of the deltoid muscle, Gal.2.354. Adv. Ruf.Oss.10

δελφάκειος.definition: of a ribs of pork, Pherecr.108.16, cf. Alex.124.2; Dieuch. ap. Orib.4.6.1

δελφάκιον.definition: Dim. of sucking-pig, Ar.Th.237; pudenda muliebria, Hsch

δελφακόομαι.definition: Pass., grow up to pighood, Ar.Ach.786

Δελφίνιον.definition: temple of Apollo Delphinios; larkspur, Delphinium Ajacis, Ps.-Dsc.3.73, Gp.20.2.2

δελφινόσημος.definition: bearing a dolphin as a device, Lyc.658

δελφινοφόρος.definition: bearing dolphins, A.Fr.150; carrying II, Th.7.41, cf. Pherecr.12

δενδρίον.definition: Dim. of Agathocl.6; Aeol. form of prob. in Alc.44, Theoc.29.12

δενδρίτης.definition: of a tree; f.l. in Hsch

δενδρόκομος.definition: grown with wood, E.Hel.1107; tree-tending, Nonn.D.47.182, 199

δενδροκοπέω.definition: cut down trees, esp. vines and fruit- trees, X.Mem.2.1.13; to waste a country by cutting down the trees, Decr. Byz. ap. D.18.90:—Pass., Corn.ND30

δενδροκόπιον.definition: tree-cutting, name of a festival, Herzog Koische Forschungen p.133

δενδρολίβανον.definition: rosemary, Rosmarinus officinalis, Gal.12.67, Aët.1.130, Gp.11.15 tit

δενδροτομέω.definition: cut down trees, Str.14.6.5; lay waste a country, Th.1.108: metaph., Ar.Pax747

δενδροφορέω.definition: to bear trees in procession, Artem.2.37

δενδροφόρος.definition: bearing trees, Theodor. ap; in pl., tree-bearers, a guild in the cult of Cybele, IGRom.1.614 ; freq. in Lat. Inscrr., cf. Lyd.Mens.4.59

δενδρόφυτος.definition: planted with trees, Plu.Cam.16; a kind of agate, with tree-like marks, Orph.L.232

δενδρύφιον.definition: Dim. of M.Ant.4.20, Dsc.1.108; toy tree, HeroSpir.1.41, al.; of corals, Thphr.HP4.7.2

δεξιάζω.definition: in Pass., = LXX2 Ma.4.34; Med., approve, PLips.41.5

δεξίμηλος.definition: receiving sheep, i.e. rich in sacrifices, E.Andr.129 , 1138, Ph.632

δεξιόσειρος ἵππος.definition: right-hand trace-horse in team of four, which did the hardest work: hence, generally, vigorous, impetuous, S.Ant.140

δεξιοστάτης.definition: one who stands in the right file of the Chorus, Poll.2.161, 4.106

δεξιότοιχος.definition: on the starboard side of a ship, AB91, Hsch

δεξιοφύλαξ.definition: right rear flank man, Hsch. s.v

δεξίωσις.definition: offer of the right hand, greeting, Ph.1.478, 2.124 , Plu.Alex.9 , Pomp.79; canvassing, ib.67 : metaph., greeting, Dam.Pr.83

δερμάτινος.definition: of skin, leathern, Od.4.782; Hdt.7.79; Arist.Fr.335; Str.16.4.19; Ev.Marc.1.6; IG5.1390.23 ; Inscr.Prien.114.11,30 ; Ph.1.100; , Porph.Abst.2.46

δερματόπτερος.definition: with wings of skin, of the bat, Ar.Byz.Epit.120.7

δερματοφορέω.definition: wear a skin or hide, Sch.A.R.1.324

δερματόω.definition: in Pass., to be turned into hide, Hsch. s.v

δερμόπτερος.definition: with membranous wings, as a bat, Arist.HA487b22, 490a7, Ael.NA11.37

δεσμέω.definition: = , Ev.Luc.8.29, Hld.8.9:—Pass., Diog.Oen.39, Luc.JTr.20, Alex.Aphr.Pr.1.75, 106; of joints, undergo ankylosis, Gal.15.410

δέσμη.definition: package, bundle, Test. ap. D.35.34; a measure in Egypt, PFay.119.4, al.; POxy.1212.4

δέσμιος.definition: binding: metaph., binding as with a; Pass., bound, captive, S.Aj.299, Ph.608, E.Ba.226, POxy.580 , etc.; on leash, prob. in Aen. Tact.31.32; = E.Ba.792

δεσμοφυλακεία.definition: tax for maintenance of prisons, PFay.53.6; service as warder, PFlor. 253 , al

δεσμωτήριον.definition: prison, Th.6.60, Pl.Grg.486a, D.9.60, etc.; Hdt.3.23: pl., = Lat.ergastula, Plu.TG8

δεσμώτης.definition: prisoner, captive, Hdt.3.143; as Adj., in chains, fettered, A.Pr.119 : fem. S.Aj.234 ; name of a play by E

δεσπόζω.definition: mostly pres. and impf.: fut. A.Pr.210; abs., to be lord or master, gain the mastery, A.Pr.210; Pl.Phd.80a, al.: as law-term, to be the legal proprietor, opp. PTheb.Bank1.15, cf. BGU1187.9 , PLond.3.977.32

δεσπόσυνος.definition: also Pi.P.4.267:—of or belonging; Subst., = Tyrt.6.2 , Anaxandr.41.33 , GDI4334

δεσποτεύω.definition: = LXX3 Ma.5.28, CIG3702 , D.C.60.28: c. gen., enjoy ownership of . ., PGen.60.1

δεσποτέω.definition: = c. gen., Pl.Ti.44d:—Pass., to be despotically ruled, A.Ch.104; E.Heracl.884; opp. A.Eu.527 , cf. 696

δεσπότις.definition: = voc. Limen.39; acc. S.Tr.407, El.597, E.Med.17, Pl.Ti.34c, Epicur.Ep.3p.65U.; gen. POxy.48.7 ; dat. AP160.8

δευτεραγωνιστής.definition: actor who takes second-class; metaph., seconder, supporter, D.19.10, Luc.Peregr.36

δευτεραῖος.definition: on the second day, usu. agreeing with the subject of the Verb, Hdt.6.106, cf. X.Cyr.5.2.2, etc.; also Hdt.4.113

δευτερεῖος.definition: of second quality, Dsc.1.49; neut. pl. , second prize in a contest, hence second place or rank, Hdt.1.32; votes for second place, Id.8.123, cf. Pl.Phlb.22c, etc.:—later in sg., CIG2360.29 , 2759 , D.L.2.133

δευτερέσχατος.definition: last but one, Heliod. ap. Orib.46.11.23

δευτερεύω.definition: to be second, Plb.18.55.5; D.S.1.73, cf. Str.8.6.18; to be next best to it, Dsc.3.39, cf. Herod.Med. ap. Orib.10.11.3; to play second to . ., Plu.Eum.13, cf. LXXEs.4.8

δευτερέω.definition: = foreg., v.l. in ib.Je52.24, cf. Hld.10.6

δευτερίας.definition: seconds, a poor wine made from Dsc.5.6, Poll.1.248, 6.17, Hsch.; prob. l. in Nicopho20

δευτέριος.definition: of inferior quality, Nicoph.20; or afterbirth, Aq.De.28.57, prob. in Paul.Aeg.6.75

δευτεροβόλος.definition: shedding the teeth a second time, Hierocl.Facet.4, cf. Hippiatr.20, POxy.1708.10 ; of camels, BGU 1088.4 , etc

δευτεροδέομαι.definition: Pass., to be secondary, produced by repetition, of numbers, Theol.Ar.22; Nicom.Ar.1.19, cf. Syrian.in Metaph.149.23:—hence Subst. , secondary series, Theol.Ar.34

δευτερόλεπτον.definition: Astron., second of a minute of degree, Rhetor. in Cat.Cod.Astr.7.194.22

δευτερολογέω.definition: speak a second time, LXX2 Ma.13.22

δευτερονόμιον.definition: second or repeated Law, the fifth book of the Pentateuch, LXX, cf. De.17.18, Jo.9.5

δευτεροστάτης.definition: one who stands in the rear; in pl., soldiers in the rear rank, Arr.Alan.17

δευτερόφωνος.definition: speaking after one, of Echo, Nonn.D.2.119

δέχνυμαι.definition: poet. for Orph.A.564, Parth.Fr.4, AP9.553; Epic.inArch.Pap.7.5, IG3.1347, Coluth.159, Q.S.12.585: in late Prose, Hld.3.2

δηληγατεύω.definition: assign as tax to be paid, PLips.64.3

δήλημα.definition: mischief, bane, Od.12.286; A.Fr.123; h.Ap.364, cf. S.OT1495; IPE2.197

δηλητήριος.definition: noxious, SIG 37 (Teos, v B; poison, Hp.Ep.19 , Plu.2.662c, Hdn.1.17.10, Lib.Or.64.33; Porph.Abst.3.8

δήλομαι.definition: Dor. for Theoc.5.27, Ti.Locr.94d, Archyt. ap. Stob.3.1.105, Plu.2.219d, Tab.Heracl.1.146, Chron.Lind.D.66, GDI 3585.18 : also Elean = Michel 1334.5

δηλόω.definition: —Pass., fut. Th.1.144; in; make known, disclose, reveal, A.Pers.519, S.OT77, etc.; prove, Id.OC146, Th.1.3; . . Democr.7; D.19.157; explain, set forth, Th.2.62; signify, gave no sign of knowing, Id.4.68: indicate, Id.…

δημαγωγία.definition: control or leader-ship of the people, Ar.Eq.191, Th.8.65, Arist.Pol.1305b23, Ath.28.4, Luc.Dem.Enc.19; demagogic method, Plb.2.21.8

δημαγωγός.definition: popular leader, as Cleon or Pericles; more freq. in bad sense, leader of the mob, demagogue, X.HG2.3.27; Plb.3.80.3; opp. And.4.27; Arist.Pol.1313b40, cf. 1292a20, etc

δημαρχέω.definition: to be at Athens, Is.12.11, D.57.26; at Chios, Schwyzer687 A 3; or tribune at Rome, App.BC1.2: pf. Arr.Epict.3.14.12

δημεραστής.definition: friend of the people, Pl.Alc.1.132a, D.C.47.38:— hence Subst. Poll.3.65, and Adj. friendly to the people, Procl.in Alc.p.146 C

δήμευσις.definition: confiscation of property, IG12.101.7, cf. Pl.Prt.325c , D.17.15; alone, Arist.Pol.1298a6; D.21.43; SIG167.26

δημηγορέω.definition: practise speaking in the assembly; esp. make popular speeches, use clap-trap, Pl.Grg.482c: abs., ib.503b, Tht.162d, R.350e; D.21.202; Id.3.3,4.38, cf. Hermog.Meth.1

διακληρόω.definition: Dor. assign by lot, allot; choose by lot, X.Cyr.6.3.36; of decimating soldiers, App.BC2.47:—Med. c. acc., ib.18, Iamb.Myst.1.5, al.: but usu. abs., cast lots, Th.8.30, X.Cyr.6.3.34; D.59.103

διακλύζω.definition: wash, wash out, E.IT107; Ath.9.381b:-Med., wash out one’s mouth, Hp.Epid.7.2, Arist.Pr.948a2; use a clyster, Hp.Aff.27:-Pass., to be washed out, with hot water, Arist.GA739b12

διάκλυσμα.definition: lotion for washing out the mouth, Gal.11.839; to prevent toothache, Dsc.1.43, cf. 96, Apollonius ap.Gal.12.864, cf. Id.11.879

διακναίω.definition: scrape or grate away, gouge out his; wear out, wear away, Hp.Morb.1.13; Ar.Ec.957, cf.E.IA27 , Heracl.296 ; murder Orestes , Stratt.1:—Pass., to be worn quite away, destroyed, A.Pr.94,541 , cf. E.Med.164 , Alc.109 ; A…

διακολακεύομαι.definition: vie with each other in flattery, Isoc.12.159:—Act. only as v.l. in Sch.E.Or.714

διακολάπτω.definition: dress stone with a chisel, Agath.2.19:-also IG7.3073.185

διακολυμβάω.definition: dive and swim across, IG12.653.29 ; Plb.5.46.8, cf. LXX1 Ma.9.48, Palaeph.27; D.S.14.116

διακονέω.definition: Ion. impf. E.Cyc.406; to be a deacon, 1 Ep.Ti.3.10,13

διακονίομαι.definition: Pass., roll in the dust, Hp.Ep.27 : hence, prepare for combat, Plu.2.970f

διακοντίζομαι.definition: Att. fut. contend with others at throwing the javelin, X.Cyr.1.4.4; Thphr.Char.27.13; simply, hurl darts, J.BJ4.3.12, 5.7.3

διακόπτω.definition: cut in two, cut through; break through the enemy's line, X.An.1.8.10; Plu.Pyrrh.7; Aen. Tact.32.7: abs., break through the enemy's line, X.HG7.5.23, etc.; Id.Cyr.3.3.66; so, of a weapon, Luc.Nigr.37: metaph. of a reme…

διακορεύω.definition: deflower, Ar.Th.480, Ephor.164, Sor.1.8, Luc.DMeretr.11.2, Artem.2.65

διακορής.definition: = Pl.Lg.629b, Max.Tyr.7.6, D.C.61.13, Jul.Or.2.65d: abs., Plu.Lyc.15

διακόρησις.definition: deflowering, prob.l. in J.AJ7.8.1, Sor.1.33, Sch.Il.18.493

διάκοσμος.definition: battle-order, Th.4.93; the Catalogue of ships in Il.2, Str.12.3.5, Sch.Il.Oxy.221 vi 22

διακούω.definition: fut. Act.Ap.23.35:—hear out or to the end, X.Oec.11.1; Men.Epit.471: abs., of a court, try out a case, OGI335.71 ; hear or learn from another, Pl.Ep.338d; Theopomp.Hist.244; Arist.Pol.1273a10: c. gen. rei, Pl.Prm.126c…

διακράτησις.definition: holding fast, retention, Sor.1.36, cf. Dsc.Ther.Praef.; control, Iamb.Myst.1.9; possession, Sch.Th.1.139, Suid. v. dub. in Eun.Hist.p.252 D

διακριβεία.definition: minute observance of the law, LXX3 Ki.11.33

διακριβόω.definition: portray exactly, APl.4.204; examine or discuss minutely or with precision, X.Cyr.2.1.27; Arist.SE169b15, cf.EN1178a23:—Med., Pl.Tht.184d; Isoc.4.18:—Pass., the subject has been examined minutely, Arist.Rh.1366a21, cf.…

διακριτής.definition: official in charge of revision of arrears of taxation, PGiss.58 ii 11 : pl., BGU734ii6

διάκρουσις.definition: putting off, to gain time, D.54.27; delay, evasion, Plu.Cor.19: pl., Id.Cic.7; escape from, Lib.Or.14.19

διακυβερνάω.definition: steer through, pilot, Pl.Ti.42e, Lg.709b; Plu.2.1026f; ib.712b; PLond.1.42.16 ; of a physician, Arist.Pr.859a18:—Pass., Iamb.Myst.8.3

διακυμαίνω.definition: raise into waves, Luc.DMar.15.4, cf. Icar.26

διακυνοφθαλμίζομαι.definition: Med., to look askance one at another, Com. Adesp.975, cf. Ael.Dion.Fr.124

διακωδωνίζω.definition: strengthd. for Lys.Fr.313S; bruit abroad, Str.2.3.4

διακωλύω.definition: hinder, prevent, Hdt.8.144, cf. Lys.20.36; E.Hec.148; Antipho5.82; Pl.Ap.31e; Th.8.92, Ev.Matt.3.14; Pl.Ep.315d; D.S.20.79; S.OC1771 ; Alc.Com.3, cf. Arist.EN1159b6:-Pass., Th.1.101; Antipho3.2.7: D.18.60

διακωμῳδέω.definition: satirise, Pl.Grg.462e, Arist.Po.1458b6, Jul.Or.6.203a: abs., D.H.Dem.57

διαλαγχάνω.definition: divide or part by lot, Hdt.4.68, A.Th.789; obtain a share by inheritance, Leg.Gort.8.4,24; obtain by lot, D.H.3.48

διαλαιμοτομέομαι.definition: Pass., have one's throat cut, Mnesim.4.16

διαλαλία.definition: verbal order, Lyd.Mag.3.67; = Lat. interlocutio, Just.Nov.126.1, Cod.Just.4.20.16, PLond.5.1674.45

διαλαμβάνω.definition: grasp or lay hold of separately, . . Hdt.4.94: hence, seize, arrest, Id.1.114, Pl.R.615e; Hdt.4.68, cf. Ar.Ec.1090

διάλαμψις.definition: shining through, Arist.Mete.369b15; Aeol. and Dor. form of Hellenistic = repute, Schwyser 647.28 ; appreciation, SIG 721.25

διαλανθάνω.definition: fut. Isoc.3.16, and as v.l. in; abscond, BGU1187.23 , PSI4.285.11

διαλείπω.definition: intermit, Id.GA757b4: esp. of Time, having left an interval of . ., Hdt.3.157, D.20.8; having waited an instant, Ar.Nu.496; Isoc.5.8; Arist.Pol.1299a37; later in gen., Hdn.7.8.9; so after a short time, Th.5.10: abs., …

διαλεπτολογέομαι.definition: discourse subtly, 'chop logic', with one, Ar.Nu.1496

διαλεπτύνω.definition: make thin, pare away, fine down, Hp.Fract.11; grind small, Sch.E.Ph.1159:—Pass., become thin, watery, of a fluid, Ruf.Sat.Gon.15:— hence Subst. Aët.16.55

διαληκάομαι.definition: laugh at, Ael.Dion.Fr.125:—hence a game, Theognost. in AB1353a

διαλιμπάνω.definition: = intermit, Gal.17.220, Mich.in EN560.1, v.l. in Act.Ap.8.24

διαλινάω.definition: slip through a net, Phryn.PSp.64 B.:—Med., Eust.574.31

διαλλαγή.definition: change, D.C.47.5, 48.53; A.D.Synt.259.25: but esp; difference, D.H.Isoc.11

διαλλακτήρ.definition: mediator, A.Th.908 , OGI 43.2 , D.H.2.76, App.Mac.4, Poll.1.153

διαλλάσσω.definition: Med., interchange, Hdt.9.47, cf. Pi.O.11.21: abs., make an exchange, X.Cyr.8.3.32, Test.Epict.2.14

διαλογίζομαι.definition: pf. Amphis33.9:—balance; calculate exactly, . . Diph.43.15, cf. Amphis l.c.; consider, Democr.112, cf. Isoc.6.90, Men.Epit.36; ib.347; Is.7.45; stop to consider, D.18.98; distinguish between, Aeschin.1.18

διαλογισμός.definition: balancing of accounts, D.36.23; calculation, consideration, Pl.Ax.367a; Str.5.3.7; this consideration, Phld.D.1.15

διαλοιδορέομαι.definition: rail furiously at, D.21.86.—Act. only in late authors, v.l. in Lib.Decl.40.11

διαλυγίζω.definition: twist about, and bend, both in Hsch

διάλυσις.definition: separating, parting; ending, cessation, E.Ph.435; Th.4.19, v.l. in Isoc.6.51: abs., cessation of hostilities, Com.Adesp.21.23 D.; settlement, compromise, IG12.6.20 , PAmh.2.63.9 , etc.: in pl., settlement of a dispute…

διάλυτος.definition: relaxed, Plu.2.136b; capable of dissolution, Pl.Phd.80b, v.l. in Ti.57b, Ph.1.495; = Phld.D.3.9

διαλύω.definition: fut. etc., loose one from another, part; dissolve into its elements, break up, destroy, Pl.R.609a s1.; Id.Ti.68d; disperse, break up a herd of sheep, BGU1012.12 ; break up a ship, IG2.804, cf. PSI4.382 ; SIG2588.169,1…

διαλωβάομαι.definition: Dep. strengthd. for Plb.11.7.2: pf. part. Pass., in pass. sense, Plu.Caes.68: metaph., Id.2.986e.—Act. only late, Mich.in EN503.21

διαμαθύνω.definition: grind to powder, utterly destroy, A.Ag.824; Id.Fr.244

διαμαλάττω.definition: strengthd. for Sor.1.118, Luc.Prom.13:— Med., Hp.Steril.221

διαμαντεύομαι.definition: determine by an oracle, Pl.Lg.696a; consult an oracle, D.H.3.69, Plu.2.302d

διαμαρτάνω.definition: fut. D.19.151:—strengthd; fail utterly of, fail of obtaining, Th.2.78; Isoc.4.93; Is.6.52; D.18.30; not to miss both of two good things, Id.19.151

διαμαρτία.definition: total mistake, Plu.Fab.6; gross fault, Ph.1.345, cf. Plu.2.153b; guilty passion, Philostr.VA1.13: pl., faults, . . Phld.Lib.p.19O

διαμαρτυρέω.definition: as Att. law-term, use a; c. inf., affirm by a that . ., . . Is.3.3, cf. D.44.48:—Pass., aor. to be affirmed in a to be so and so, Lys.23.13, cf. Is.3.5; Isoc.18.15

διαμαρτύρομαι.definition: generally, protest, asseverate, Pl.Phd.101a, etc., PSI4.422 : c. acc., bear witness to, Act.Ap.20.24; testify, LXXDe.32.46, al.; ib.Ez.16.2

διαμασάομαι.definition: chew up, Arist.HA612a1, Thphr.CP6.9.1; metaph., carp at, Philostr.VSPraef

διαμάσημα.definition: that which is chewed, Hp.Aff.4, Dsc.1.96

διαμάσσω.definition: Att. bake to a turn, - Ar.Eq.1105: metaph., Id.Av.463

διαμαστιγόω.definition: scourge severely, Phld.Rh.2.298 S.:—Pass., bear marks of scourging, Pl.Grg.524c

διαμαστίγωσις.definition: severe scourging, esp. of the Spartan boys, Plu.2.239d

διαμαστροπεύω.definition: pander: metaph. in Pass., bargained away by a marriage, Plu.Caes.14

διαμάχη.definition: a fight, struggle, Pl.Lg.633d, cf. J.BJ6.2.8 , Ph.1.7, al., Plu.2.74c, etc

διαμάχομαι.definition: exert oneself, strive earnestly, . . Pl.Prt.325d; . . Id.Grg.502b

διαμεθίημι.definition: leave off, E.Ba.627; give up, Id.El.978

διαμείβω.definition: exchange, one thing with another; finish a journey, A.Th.334 :—Med., Id.Pr.287 ; but in Med. also, pass through, Id.Supp.543 ; Id.Fr.150

διαμελετάω.definition: practise diligently, Pl.Prm.126c:—Med., Max.Tyr.7.7:—Pass., Pl.Lg.830b, cf. Sm.Ps.76.13: c. inf., Iamb.Protr.20

διαμέλλησις.definition: postponement, procrastination, long postponement of precautionary measures, Th.5.99, cf. D.C.Fr.40.21

διαμέλλω.definition: fut. to be always going to do, to make a show of doing: hence, delay, put off, Th.1.71,142, Ph.1.353, Luc.Nigr.10, al.:—Pass., Th.8.54

διαμέμφομαι.definition: blame greatly, Th.8.89; Isoc.3.1; D.C.46.51; . . Arist.PA663a35

διαμένω.definition: fut. Epich.[265] , Men.Epit.513: aor. D.4.15: pf. Plb.3.55.1:—continue, persist, of disease, Hp.Aph.3.28; X.Cyr.8.2.7: abs., keep, of seeds, Thphr.HP7.5.5; persevere, Pl.Prt.344b; X.Ap.30; maintain his purpose, Plb.10…

διαμερίζω.definition: divide, Pl.Phlb.15e; distribute; part, separate, Men.883:—Med., divide or part among themselves, Ev.Matt.27.35; PAmh.2.152.18 :—Pass., to be set at variance, Ev.Luc.12.52,53

διαμέτρησις.definition: measuring out, LXX2 Ch.3.3; Astron., diametrical opposition, Ptol.Tetr.195, etc

διάμετρος.definition: diametrical: Astrol., diametrically; Subst. , diagonal of a parallelogram, Pl.Men.85b,al.; of triangles, by the hypotenuses, Id.Ti.54d; diameter of a circle, Arist.Cael.271a12, etc.; axis of a sphere, Id.MA699a29; dia…

διαμηρίζω.definition: femora diducere, inire, Ar.Av.669, Zeno Stoic.1.59

διαμίγνυμι.definition: or , fut. to mix up, l.c.:— Pass., Pl.Com.174.9 codd. Ath.; cf

διαμιλλάομαι.definition: fut. Str.17.1.11:—contend hotly, strive earnestly, Pl.Lg.833e; with one, Id.R.516e; Plb.16.21.6; about a thing, Pl.R.517d; ib.563a: c. gen. rei, Id.Lg.833b; Plu.Them.5: pf. in pass. sense, Luc.Par.58

διαμιμνῄσκομαι.definition: only pf. Pass. keep in; make mention of, Ph.1.509, Lyd.Mag.1.7

διαμισέω.definition: hate bitterly, Arist.Pol.1274a34, Ph.1.396, J.BJ4.5.4, Plu.Tim.35 , Ant.Lib.12.2

διαμισθόω.definition: farm out, PAmh.2.95.7, al., OGI669.14 , etc.:—Med., App.BC2.10

διαμίσθωσις.definition: farming out of state land, PTeb.72.450 , 376.15

διαμνημονεύω.definition: remember distinctly, abs., Hdt.3.3; mention, record, Th.1.22; he is mentioned as having, X.Cyr.1.1.2

διαμονομαχέω.definition: fight a single combat, Plu.2.482c, cf. Hld.7.16

διαμορφόω.definition: give form to, shape, Ph.2.368; Plu.Rom.16:—Pass., articulate, Id.2.722c, cf. Ath.Med. ap. Orib.22.9.4

διαμυθολογέω.definition: communicate by word of mouth, express in speech, A.Pr.889 ; Pl.Lg.632e; converse, Id.Ap.39e; Id.Phd.70b; tell a story, Max.Tyr.16.1

διαμφισβητέω.definition: dispute, disagree, Decr. ap.D.18.185, cf. Arist.MM1211a14; Ath.8.351a; Plu.2.787d; lay claim to, Arist.Pol.1283b14; ib.1287b35; Id.PA648a24: abs., Id.Pol.1283a30, CPR1.20 , etc.:—Pass., not a few questions are debatea…

διαμφισβήτησις.definition: disputing, . . it admits of dispute whether . ., Arist.Pol.1256a14; contain ambiguous points, of Solon's laws, Id.Ath.35.2; disputed territory, SIG685.55 ; . . Plu.Tim.Praef.: pl., Iamb.Myst.4.1

διαμφοδέω.definition: miss the right Eust.789.54: metaph., miss the right way , S.E.M.9.31, cf. Hsch. s.v

διαμωκάομαι.definition: mock or laugh at, Phld.Rh.2.59S., D.C.59.25, Iamb.VP33.234: abs., Aristaenet.1.27

διαναγιγνώσκω.definition: read through, Isoc.12.201, Plb.31.21.9; Damox.2.13:—Pass., D.C.58.10

διαναγκάζω.definition: drill, train, Pl.Lg.836a ; reduce dislocation, Hp.Mochl.38; force open the pores, Id.Vict.2.64:—Pass., to be dilated, Id.Fist.4

διαναγκασμός.definition: = foreg.; machine for this purpose, Id.Art.47

διαναπαύω.definition: allow to rest awhile, Hp.Aph.2.48, Arist.Pol.1339b30, Plu.Flam.4; interrupt, Luc.Am.7; relieve the monotony, D.H.Comp.12:—Med., rest awhile, Pl.Lg.625b, Ph.2.197, Porph.Marc.4:—also intr. in Act., Aristid.Or.51.17

διαναρμοστέω.definition: to be out of time, Poll.4.63

διανάστασις.definition: rising up, Hp.Epid.7.11 , Plb.5.70.8: pl., X.Cyn.10.18

διαναστρέφομαι.definition: to be distorted, roll, of the eyes, Herod.Med. in Rh.Mus.58.78

διαναυμαχέω.definition: maintain a sea-fight, Hdt.8.63, Th.8.27; Isoc.4.97

διανάω.definition: flow through, percolate, Plu.Aem.14; cf. Hsch

διανδραγαθέω.definition: continue to behave honourably, Wilcken Chr.10.3 , BGU1204.6

διανεμόομαι.definition: Pass., flutter in the wind, Luc.Im.7, AP9.777 ; to be blown away by the wind, Eun.Hist.p.269D

διανήχομαι.definition: = Hellanic.111J., J.AJ13.1.3, Plu.Luc.10, Ael.NA6.15, Palaeph.30, Porph.Abst.2.5; of sound, penetrate, Erinna3: metaph., Vett. Val.68.12

διανθίζω.definition: adorn with flowers, Luc.Bis Acc.16 ; also with jewels, J.AJ8.5.2:—Pass., to be picked out, decorated, Plu.Phil.9; Paus.6.19.12; Id.7.26.4, cf. Hdn.5.3.6; of a leper, Ph.1.346

διανίζω.definition: wash out or thoroughly, Crates Com.14.7, Eub.31, Damox.2.44; Diocl.Fr.139:—Med., Hp.Mul.2.112

διανίσσομαι.definition: go through, Pi.P.12.25, Opp.H.1.550: Ep. Subj. Orph.Fr.285.56

διανίστημι.definition: fut. awaken, rouse, D.H.4.2; Pass., with aor. 2 and pf. Act., stand up, rise, Arist.Oec.1345a16; spring up from ambush, Plb.3.74.1, cf. PPetr.2p.59 , D.S.10.1, Plu.2.596a, etc

διανοέω.definition: have in mind, Philostr.Im.2.1:—but in early; have in mind, Hp.VM7; what he really meant by his words, Pl.Tht.184a; Id.Lg.644d, 686d: c. acc. et inf., think or suppose that . ., Id.Prt.324b, etc.: c. gen. abs., Id.R.47…

διανόημα.definition: thought, notion, X.HG7.5.19, Isoc.3.9, Pl.Smp.210d; Plu.2.40c; thought, opp. words, Pl.Prt.348d, Phld.Po.2.30,40: pl., meanings of words, Id.Rh.2.190S.; esp. whim, sick fancy, Hp.Epid.1.23; intention, PLond.5.1724.15,…

διανοητής.definition: one who thinks, gloss on Hsch

διανομοθετέω.definition: get a motion carried and made law; regulate by law, Id.38.7:—Med., Pl.Lg.833e

διανοσέω.definition: in aor. fall ill, Hp.Epid.3.6, Gal.Thras.7

διαντλέω.definition: drain, exhaust: only metaph., drink to the dregs, endure to the end, Pi.P.4.293; E.Andr.1217 ; Id.HF1373; Ph.1.161; Luc.Pseudol.25: abs., Heraclit.Incred.21:—Pass., Pl.Mx.241e, cf. Lib.Or.59.94

διαντλίζομαι.definition: Pass., exhaust oneself, to be worried or troubled, Hp.Praec.7

διανυκτερεύω.definition: pass the night, X.HG5.4.3, cf. PTeb.268.73 : abs., Ph.2.488, Plu.Aem.16, al.; Ev.Luc.6.12, cf. Hdn.1.16.5

διαξαίνω.definition: aor. Gp.2.6.42, but inf; metaph., of the wind, Hld.3.3; Opp.H.5.306; as a punishment, Ael.Fr.131:—Pass., ib.130

διαπαιδαγωγέω.definition: attend children: generally, guide, Pl.Ti.89d; entertain, amuse, Plu.Per.11; while away the time, Id.Sert.16

διαπαιδεύομαι.definition: Pass., take a course of education, X.Cyr.1.2.15

διαπαίζω.definition: late fut. Gal.8.569: pf. Plu; laugh, jest at, c.acc., J.BJ5.7.4, Arr.Epict.2.18.22, Demetr.Eloc.147, D.L.4.53: abs., Phld.Lib.p.57 O

διαπαλαίω.definition: continue wrestling, Ar.Eq.573, Ph.2.544, J.AJ1.20.2; Ach.Tat.4.19: c. dat., struggle with, Gal.17.569

διαπαραδίδωμι.definition: hand over to a successor, IG9.1109.64,91

διαπαρατηρέομαι.definition: lie in wait for continually, LXX2 Ki.3.30

διαπαρθενεύω.definition: deflower a maiden, Hdt.4.168 , Diocl.Com.16, Antiph.75, Alex.314

διαπασσαλεύω.definition: Att. stretch out by nailing the extremities, Hdt.7.33; of a hide pegged out for tanning, Ar.Eq.371, cf. Plu.Art.17

διαπάσσω.definition: Att. sprinkle, Hdt.6.125; Eub.128; Alc.Com.17; Arist.HA526a12; with red spots, ib.527b30

διαπειλέω.definition: threaten violently, Hdt.7.15; c.inf.fut., Plu.Oth.16:—Med., Aeschin.1.43, Alex.306, PPetr.2p.1: c. inf., forbid with threats, Plb.1.78.15; . . Conon50.3

διάπειρα.definition: crucial experiment, trial, proof, Hdt.2.28,77; Id.1.47; Pi.O.4.18

διαπειράζω.definition: tempt, make trial of, LXX3 Ma.5.40; attempt, try, c. inf., J.AJ15.4.2

διαπειράομαι.definition: aor. Antipho5.34: pf; attempt obstinately, Antipho l.c

διαπείρω.definition: drive through, E.Ph.26; pierce, transfix, Gp.5.36.3; Plu.Art.14; Dsc.2.61:—Pass., Plu.2.567f; J.AJ10.1.2; to be interpenetrated, of muscle and flesh, Gal.8.74

διαπέμπω.definition: send off in different directions; send over or across, Ar.Pl.398; Th.4.123; transmit, BGU5ii19 , etc.; Th.1.129:—Med., Id.3.75 , SIG741.33 ; Ph.2.43

διαπεραίνω.definition: bring to a conclusion, E.Andr.333; traverse, pass through, Aret.SA2.8

διαπεραίωσις.definition: carrying over, Sch.Th.3.76; crossing over, Marcian.Peripl.1.44

διαπερδικίζω.definition: slip through like a partridge, Com.Adesp.87

διαπερονάω.definition: pin or pierce through, D.S.4.64; Agath.1.9:—Pass., Id.2.9, al., Luc.Gall.24; D.H.9.64

διαπετάννυμι.definition: pf. D.S.17.115, Pass. ib.10:—open and spread out, Ar.Lys.732,733; of the polypus, Arist.HA541b5; D.S.17.115:—Pass., pf. prob. in Pi.Dith.Oxy.2.4

διαπέτομαι.definition: fly away, vanish, Pl.Phd.70a, 84b, etc.; of Time, E.HF507; of a report, fly in all directions, Hdn.2.8.7

διάπηγμα.definition: cross-bar, Ph.Bel.54.19, HeroBel.83.8, Dioptr.34, Heliod. ap. Orib.49.7.1; partition, HeroAut.11.9

διαπηγμάτιον.definition: Dim. of foreg., small crossbar, Ph.Bel.64.7

διαπιαίνω.definition: make very fat, in Pass., Thphr.CP6.11.7, Theoc.16.91

διαπικραίνομαι.definition: Pass., to be greatly embittered, Plu.2.457a

διαπίμπλημι.definition: aor. inf. fill full, Philostr.Im.2.27; Eun.VSp.493D., cf. Nonn.D.5.194; in early writers in Pass., to be filled with, Th.7.85; to be satiated or tired, of one, And.1.125

διαπίμπρημι.definition: burn, Plb.21.44.30; Aen. Tact.4.2 :—Pass., swell up , Nic.Al.341; Hippiatr.27

διαπιπράσκω.definition: sell off, PTeb.5.192 , etc.; Plu.Comp. Lys.Sull.3

διαπιστέω.definition: distrust utterly, D.19.324, Arist.Pol.1314a17: abs., disbelieve, PSI4.377.9 , Aps.Rh.p.287 H.:—Med., mistrust oneself, Plb.18.46.7

διαπλανάω.definition: lead quite astray, Plu.2.917e, Arr.Epict.1.20.10; deceive, cheat, BGU367 :—Pass., go astray, wander, D.S.17.116, Plu.Fr.inc.11

διάπλασμα.definition: model, shape, or perh. modelled jug, Sch.Ar.V.614

διαπλασμός.definition: v.l. for Placit.1.3.18; massage of infants, Sor.1.101

διαπλάσσω.definition: Att. form, mould, Ph.1.15; plaster, Thphr.HP4.15.2

διαπλατύνω.definition: dilate, X.Lac.2.5; fiatten out, Chrysipp.Tyan. ap. Ath.14.648a

διαπλέκω.definition: weave, plait, h.Merc.80; opp; metaph., finish the web of one's life, Pi.N.7.99; prob. in Alcm.23.38; Pl.Lg.806a, cf. Com.Adesp.231: without Ar.Av.754

διαπληκτίζομαι.definition: spar, LXXEx.2.13; Luc.Anach.11: generally, skirmish with, Plu.Luc.31: metaph., wrangle, Id.Tim.14; Id.2.760a, cf. Agath.2.29: c. dat. modi, Plu.Sull.2:—late in Act., Horap.1.70

διαπλίσσομαι.definition: stand or walk with the legs apart, long-shanked, straddling, Archil.58: so in pf. part. Act., wide open, Hp.Mul.2.167, cf. Hsch., and v. foreg

διαπλοκή.definition: intermixture, Hp.Alim.11; in pl., crooked ways, Aq.Ps.124.5

διάπνοια.definition: = foreg.I, Poll.2.219, Gp.7.6.10; opening, gap, Pall.inHp.Fract.12.283C

διαποδισμός.definition: jumping about: a kind of dance, Poll.4.99

διαποζεύγνυμαι.definition: Pass., to be utterly separated, depart, Ph.1.255

διαποικίλλω.definition: variegate, adorn with variety, mostly metaph., Hp.Vict.3.68; Isoc.9.9; literally, Plu.Sert.14:—Pass., to be dappled, Arist.HA503b5: metaph., . . to be blended of various sorts, Pl.Lg.693d, cf. 863a; Plu.Lys.7, cf. Iam…

διαπολιορκέω.definition: carry a siege to its conclusion, Th.3.17

διαπολιτεύομαι.definition: to be a political rival, Aeschin.3.194, Harp. s.v. of Thucydides son of Melesias, Marcellin.Vit. Thuc.28

διαπομπή.definition: interchange of messages, negotiation, Th.6.41 ; App.BC5.71, POxy.471.61 : sg., App.Hisp.91

διαπορεύω.definition: carry over, conduct through, X.An.2.5.18; mostly Med., with aor. Pass. across, Hdt.4.33: c. acc., go through, Th.5.52; X.An.3.3.3; Pl.Lg.845a; Satyr.Vit.Eur.Fr.39xx14; travel along a line, Arist.EN1174b1, cf. Archim.S…

διαπορθμεύω.definition: carry over or across a river or strait; metaph., transmit, Pl.Smp.202e, cf. Procl.Inst.148, Iamb.Myst.1.5; Jul.Or.2.81c

διαπόρθμιος.definition: transmitting, mediating, of certain spiritual beings, Orac. ap. Dam.Pr.339; Procl.in Cra.33 P., cf. eund. in Alc.p.69 C

διαπορπακίζω.definition: aor. inf. put the hand through the Hsch

διαποστέλλω.definition: dispatch, D.35.54, cf. Plb.5.17.9, D.S.19.30; Supp.Epigr.2.261.6 :—Pass., UPZ39.18 ; of a letter, Plb.5.42.7; of scouts, Id.18.22.2:—Med. in act. sense, IG12.32.15 , SIG692.56 ; send as a representative, POxy.286.26 ,…

διαποστολή.definition: sending of messages, Plb.5.37.3 , OGI248.58 ; D.H.7.12

διαπραγματεύομαι.definition: discuss or examine thoroughly; gain by trading, Ev.Luc.19.15

διαπρεπής.definition: distinguished, Pi.I.5.44; Th.2.34; Democr.195, cf. E.Supp.841, IA1588; Id.Antiop.ii A7A.; magnificence, Th.6.16. Adv. magnificently, Plu.Alc.12; Id.Mar.28, J.BJ7.1.2 : Sup. D.50.7

διαπρέπω.definition: appear prominent or conspicuous, strike the; to be eminent, AP9.513 ; Luc.Salt.9, cf. D.C.68.6; Plu.2.771e, D.C.42.34: c. gen., E.Alc.642

διαπρεσβεύομαι.definition: send embassies, X.HG3.2.24, cf. SIG633.121 , Plb.1.11.11, D.S.11.68, Plu.Sert.23; D.C.45.43:— later in Act., serve as envoy, PPetr.3p.150

διαπτέρωσις.definition: clearning with a feather, v.l. in Hp.Acut.58, cf. Erot

διαπτύω.definition: spit upon, Ael.NA4.22: abs., Gal.13.46: metaph., c. acc., D.18.258, cf. Lib.Or.57.53,al.; of food, Plu.2.101c; Lat.frenum respuere, Philostr.Im.2.5:—Pass., D.Chr.38.38

διάπτωμα.definition: stumble, slip, Philem.60; error, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.215, Phld.Herc.1251.5; failure, opp. Id.Po.5.21; fall in with great losses, IPE12.32.55 , cf. SIG364.62 ; loss, deficiency in accounts, PHib.1.52.9 , etc

διάπτωσις.definition: fall, Gal.18.506: chiefly metaph., failure, Epicur.Fr.556; Stoic. 3.98, cf. Phld.Lib.p.280 O., Herc.1251.7, S.E.M.7.423, Plu.2.800a, etc

διαπυΐσκομαι.definition: Pass., suppurate throughout, Hp.VC2, M.Ant.4.39:—later in Act., Aret.SD1.9

διαπυκτεύω.definition: spar, fight with, X.Cyr.7.5.53, Arr.Epict.2.21.11, etc.: abs., of cocks, Luc.Anach.37: metaph., Id.Gall.22

διαπυνθάνομαι.definition: ), search out by questioning, find out, . . Pl.Smp.172a, etc.; something from one, Plu.Cat.Mi.16; . . Pl.R.469a: abs., Id.Hp.Mi.369d

διαπυριάομαι.definition: Pass., to be thoroughly heated, Hp.Steril.234

διαπυρίζω.definition: heat thoroughly:—Pass., metaph., glow with anger, Hsch

διαπυρόομαι.definition: set on fire, E.Cyc.694: Pass., metaph., Plu.Phoc.6; to be consumed with thirst, LXX4 Ma.3.15

διαπυρσεύω.definition: communicate by beacon, App.Mith.79: metaph., blazon abroad as by beacon-fires, Plu.Demetr.8: c.gen., Philostr.VA2.22 : —Med., make signals by beacons, Plb.1.19.7

διαπωλέω.definition: sell publicly, X.HG4.6.6, Plu.Oth.4; sell entirely, PLips.35.17 :—Pass., SIG695.62

διάρθρωσις.definition: esp. movable articulation, diarthrosis , Gal.2.735, 18.433; of the voice, articulate utterance, Arist.HA535a31; Id.PA660a22

διαρκέω.definition: in point of Time, endure, last, A.Th.842 ; Pl.Ti.21d: c. part., X.HG5.3.21; Arist.Mete.352b4; Plu.Fab.27; Luc.Hist.Conscr.21

διαρκής.definition: lasting, D.3.33; D.H.6.54: Comp., Luc.Anach.24: Sup., with staying power, of an athlete, Paus.6.13.3; Them.Or.11.146a. Adv. S.E.P.3.115, Eun.Hist.p.209D., Demoph.Sent.10, etc.; to be amply provided with, Procop.Pers.1…

διαρραίνω.definition: pf. LXXPr.7.17:—sprinkle; Pass., to be diffused, dissipated, S.Tr.14, Arist.Mete.341a30

διαρράπτω.definition: sew through or together, Str.15.1.67, Plu.2.978a; insert a suture, Gal.18.746

διαρρήγνυμι.definition: break through, Hom. only in Med., Il.12.308; having broken the bridle asunder, Thgn.259; . . Hdt.3.12; . . having cloven it, S.Aj.834; Pl.Phd.86a:—Pass., burst, as with eating, X.Cyr.8.2.21, Anaxil.25, Phoenicid.3, et…

διαρρικνόομαι.definition: draw up and twist the body, of an unseemly kind of dance, Cratin.219

διαρρινάω.definition: file through or perforate, HeroAut.25.5, Sor.2.63: pf. part. Pass. perforated, Arist.Ath.68.3, cf. Dsc.4.114: metaph., fine, critical, Max.Tyr.36.4

διαρρίνησις.definition: filing through, perforation, Heliod. ap. Orib.47.17.4

διαρροΐζομαι.definition: suffer from diarrhoea, Dsc.4.88, Arr.Epict.4.10.11, Alex.Aphr.Pr.1.98

διαρρομβέομαι.definition: assume the figure of a rhombus, HeroMetr.1.16

διαρρυθμίζω.definition: adjust, IG12.373.70; arrange in order, LXX2 Ma.7.22

διαρταμέω.definition: strengthd. for cut limb-meal, A.Pr.1023, Anaxandr.6; is cj. in Ph.2.564

διαρτάω.definition: suspend, Hsch., dub. l. for; keep in suspense, keep engaged, in or by . ., D.H.1.46; mislead, deceive, Men.1006

διαρτίζω.definition: mould, form, LXXJb.33.6; speak fitly, Hsch

διάρτισις.definition: moulding, shaping, EM361.8, Suid.; composition, prob. l. for Gal.15.102

διασαλακωνίζω.definition: strengthd. for Ar.V.1169; but perh. better cf. Id.Fr.849

διασαλεύω.definition: shake violently, Plb.1.48.2, Luc.VH2.5; of; confuse, D.H.Comp.22,23; cause excitement in, Luc.Alex.31; negligent, easy in gait, Id.Rh.Pr.11; of an ogler, Id.Merc.Cond.35

διασάττω.definition: stuff with a thing, Gal.1.32: pf. part. Pass. Archig. ap. eund.8.931; c. gen., gorged with . ., Macho ap.Ath.6.244c: c. gen., Gp.19.9.5: c. dat., Ruf. ap. Orib.8.24.13

διασαφέω.definition: make quite clear, show plainly, E.Ph.398; Pl.Lg.916e, Phld.Lib.p.13 O., etc.; . . Pl.Prt.348b, cf. Phld.Po.5.13; also make a clear statement about . ., Arist.de An.404b1; send clear information . ., Plb.3.87.4; Id.2.1…

διασαφηνίζω.definition: make clear, X.Mem.3.1.11, Ap.1; D.H.11.33, cf. Aët.13.15:—Pass., HeroBel.98.6

διασεισμός.definition: abuse of power, extortion, PTaur.1v1 , cf. PTeb.43.36 , POxy. 1252133

διάσειστος.definition: shaken about, Aeschin.1.59, cf. Men.423; Poll.7.203

διασείω.definition: shake violently, Hp.Morb.1.6, dub. in; confound, throw into confusion, Hdt.6.109; Plb.18.45.2; intimidate, oppress, Id.10.26.4, cf. OGI519.14 ; browbeat, PTaur.1viii13 ; extort money by intimidation from a person, PPa…

διασήθω.definition: aor. sift, Hp.VM3, Dsc.5.75; prob. for Diocl. ap. Orib.8.41.3:—Pass., Aret.CA2.3

διασημειόομαι.definition: cause to be placed on record, Inscr. Magn.117.3

διάσημος.definition: clear, distinct: neut. pl. as; conspicuous, eminent, Hippias Soph.4 , Plu.Dio54; Id.TG17; BMus.Inscr. 481*.15 : esp. in Sup., Epigr.Gr.904 ; = Lat. clarissimus, IG3.635; = perfectissimus, BGU198.5 , al., Epigr.Gr.1078…

διασήπω.definition: cause to putrefy, Str.15.1.37, cf. Dsc.2.173, Gal.18.455; Ael.NA9.62:—freq.in Pass., with pf. putrefy, Thphr.HP5.7.5, Luc.Luct.18; Id.Alex.59

διασθενέω.definition: to be exhausted, of soil, POxy.1502v6

διασιλλαίνω.definition: mock, jeer at, c. acc., Luc.Lex.24; Alciphr.3.62

διασιωπάω.definition: fut. remain silent, E.Hel.1551; pause in reading, Gal.16.742, al

διασκανδικίζω.definition: prop. feed on chervil , Telecl.38: hence Com. for to come Euripides over one , Ar.Eq.19

διασκάπτω.definition: Dor. 3pl. fut. Tab.Heracl.1.131:—dig through, Paus.2.1.5; make a breach in them, Lys.13.14; make a breach for water in the canals, Tab.Heracl. l. c., cf. Ph.Bel.98.27: also c. gen., Plu.Pyrrh.33; excavate, Charito8.7

διασκαριφάομαι.definition: sketch in outline: hence, slur over; Act., scratch the ground, of birds, Hsch

διασκατόομαι.definition: Pass., to be befouled or filthy, of the Epicureans, Diog.Sinop.1

διασκεδάζω.definition: = sq., LXXPs.32.10; disperse a tumour, Aët.15.15

διασκεδαστής.definition: scatterer, as Adj., extravagant, reckless, Ph.1.89

διασκελίζομαι.definition: in pf. part. Pass., having the legs parted, PMag.Par.1.2309; Eust.1038.10, cf. EM502.39

διασκευάζω.definition: get ready, set in order; equip, Luc.Nec.16:—Pass., dressed as . ., Plu.Ant.24; Aen. Tact.26.1:—Med., prepare for oneself, provide, Th.4.38; arm, equip or prepare oneself, X.HG4.2.19; Din.1.70; prepare all one's tricks…

διασκευαστής.definition: reviser, editor of a poem, Sch.Il.6.441

διασκευή.definition: construction, Aristeas64, al; equipment, Plb.8.29.7; D.S.4.38; furniture or vessels, LXXEx.31.7, cf. Plb.30.26.3, Agatharch.8

διασκευωρέω.definition: revise, rehandle, Pl.Ep.316a:—Med., set in order, Id.R.540e

διασκηνέω.definition: separate and retire each to his billet; leave another's tent, Id.Cyr.3.1.38, dub. in Id.HG4.8.18

διασκηρίπτω.definition: prop on each side, prop up, AP6.203

διασκορπίζω.definition: scatter abroad, LXXGe.49.7 , al.:—Pass., Ev.Jo.11.52, Plb.1.47.5, BGU1049.7 ; squander, Ev.Luc.15.13; confound, ib.1.51; winnow, Ev.Matt.25.24

διασκορπισμός.definition: scattering, dispersal, LXXEz.6.8, al.; confusion, PTeb.24.55

διασκώπτω.definition: jest upon, dub. l. in Plu.2.82b; Ath.2.55d:—Med., jest one with another, bandy jests, X.Cyr.8.4.23

διασμιλεύω.definition: polish off with the chisel: metaph., AP15.38 ; refined, subtle theories, Alex.221.8. Adv. Poll.6.150, Hsch

διασοβέω.definition: scare away, Plu.2.133a; agitate, excite, Alciphr.Fr.5, Agath.3.11:—Pass., to be excited, puffed up, Plu.2.32d

διασπαθάω.definition: squander away, Plu.Cic.27; Med., plunder, rob, POxy.71ii12

διασπαράσσω.definition: Att. rend in pieces; metaph., Luc.Icar.21

διασπασμός.definition: tearing in pieces, LXXJe.15.3; interruption, interval, in pl., Plu.2.129b, etc.; complete severance, Dam.Pr.74: metaph., distraction, Phld.Ir.p.29 W

διασπάω.definition: fut. Ar.Ra.477, Ec.1076, also; in military sense, separate part of an army from the rest, X.Cyr.5.4.19; of army and fleet, Hdt.7.236; break them up, Arist.Pol.1303b13: —Pass., an army scattered and in disorder, Th.6.9…

διασπείρω.definition: aor. 2 Pass. S.El.748, etc.:—scatter or spread about, . . Hdt.3.13; dispersed us, ib.68; X.HG5.1.25; Isoc.5.104; squander, S.El.1291:—Pass., to be scattered, Id.Tr.782; Id.El.748; of troops, Th.1.11, X.HG5.3.1, etc.; …

διασποδέω.definition: sens. obsc., = Lat. subigitare, Ar.Ec.939, cf. Hsch. s.v. Id

διασπορά.definition: scattering, dispersion; collectively, = LXXDe.28.25, Ev.Jo.7.35: pl., LXXPs.146.2

διασπουδάζω.definition: do zealously:—and Pass., to be anxiously; to be zealous, D.H.Lys.14

διάσταλσις.definition: arrangement, compact, LXX2; = perh. to be read in Gal.8.736 for

διαστασιάζω.definition: form into separate factions; to be at variance, Plb.1.82.4, etc.; D.C.54.17; Iamb.Myst.9.4: abs., ib.4.9

διαστέλλω.definition: put asunder, expand, separate; divide, Pl.Plt.265e; distinguish, Sch.Il.Oxy.1086.115; POxy.1012 Fr.16.5

διαστίλβω.definition: gleam, Ar.Pax567, Nonn.D.42.420; gleam through, Ar.Fr.8, AP5.47 , Plu.2.497e

διαστοιχίζομαι.definition: Med., arrange for oneself regularly, regulate exactly, A.Pr.232

διαστολή.definition: drawing asunder, dilatation; separation, Thphr.CP3.16.3; notch or nick, Plu.Cic.1; boundary, fence, Tab.Heracl.2.46; fencing off, PAmh.2.40.25

διαστολικόν.definition: official notification of payment due, writ, POxy.68.33 , al.; in full, BGU613.18

διάστολον.definition: in pl., dispositions of a deed, PLond.1727.58

διαστρατεύομαι.definition: Med., serve through one's campaigns: a veteran, D.C.58.18

διαστρατηγέω.definition: assume the position of general; trans., to out-general, Plb.21.39.9; Dion.Byz.53

διαστρέφω.definition: turn different ways, twist about; metaph., distort, pervert, E.Fr.597; Is.11.4; Arist.Rh.1354a24; Id.EN1140b14; Phld.Lib.p.32 O.; having misrepresented it, D.Prooem.46.2:—Pass., Luc.Vit. Auct.24; perverse, LXXDe.32.5

διαστροφή.definition: twisting, of a fractured limb; metaph., perversion, Arist.EE1227a21; Plb.2.21.8, Porph.Abst.1.13, etc.; Plu.2.520c; LXXPr.2.14

διάστροφος.definition: twisted, distorted, Hdt.1.167; A.Pr.673, cf. S.Aj.447; Id.Tr.794; E.Ba.1122, cf. 1166 ; of a person, Ath.8.339f, Luc.Ind.7. Adv. incorrectly, S.E.M.1.152

διαστρώννυμι.definition: spread a couch, etc; Pass., of titles to property, to be registered, POxy.1725.17 , etc

διαστυλόω.definition: support by pillars set at intervals, Plb.5.100.4:—Pass., ib.4.8; D.S.20.23

διασυνίστημι.definition: set forth, signify clearly,237, al; introduce, bring forward, Ph.1.368, al.:—Pass., to be presented to the mind, M.Ant.3.2

διασυρίζω.definition: whistle, of the wind, LXXDa.3.50; f.l. in Theopomp.Hist.76:—also c. acc. metaph., Lib.Decl.40.59; also, whistle away, waste idly, Lyd.Mag.2.26

διασυρμός.definition: disparagement, ridicule, Phld.Vit.p.37 J., D.S.14.109, Longin.38.6, Ph.2.571 , Artem.3.25

διασύρω.definition: pf. Diph.75:— Pass., pf; break up, disperse, Plb.10.42.4

διασφαγή.definition: gap, LXXNe.4.7; v; sluice-gate, Wilcken Chr.11 B6

διασφαιρίζω.definition: throw about like a ball, E.Ba.1136

διασφαιρόομαι.definition: to be rolled up into a ball, plpf. Nonn.D.3.137

διασφαλίζομαι.definition: secure firmly, Plb.5.69.2, Ph.Byz.Mir.4.2, Herod. Med. ap. Orib.8.7.3:—Pass., J.AJ15.11.3

διασφάλλω.definition: overturn utterly, Luc.Abd.17:—Pass., to fail of, be disappointed of, Aeschin.2.35,3.91, D.S.20.10; Plb.5.81.7,4.14.3, cf. Arist.Ath.19.3; Vett.Val.116.34

διασφενδονάω.definition: scatter as by a sling, D.S.17.83:—Pass; dismember, Plu.Alex.43

διάσφιγξις.definition: binding tight, ligature, Sor.2.41, Heliod. ap. Orib.10.18, Antyll.ib.7.9.3, Aret.CA2.2

διασφυδόω.definition: cause to swell up, Hsch.; cf

διασχηματίζω.definition: shape, form variously, Str.17.1.4; simply, shape, model, Luc.Icar.6, v.l. in Prom.11

διασχημάτισις.definition: formation, i.e. dimensions, of a groove, Procl.Hyp.3.19: generally, Id.in Ti.3.261 D

διάσχισις.definition: division, cleft, Ath.11.488e; of roads, Them.Or.20.236b

διάσχισμα.definition: interval, Sch.D.T.p.191 H. (Dind; in Music, interval of half the Philol.6

διασχοινίζω.definition: scatter, in pf. part. Pass., Hsch

διασῴζω.definition: preserve through a danger, of persons; of things, preserve, maintain, . . E.Hel.65; keep in memory, X.Mem.3.5.22; Id.HG7.2.17; Pl.R.395b, cf. Arist.Ph.189b1; Isoc.10.63:—Med., preserve for oneself, retain, Th.3.39, 5.…

διαταγή.definition: command, ordinance, LXX2 Es.4.11, Ep.Rom.13.2; CIG3465, POxy.92.3 ; testamentary disposition, IGRom.4.840.3, etc.; make arrangements for . ., PFay.133.4 ; Ps.-Callisth.1.33; Act.Ap.7.53; medical regimen, Ruf. ap. Orib…

διάταγμα.definition: ordinance, edict, Phld.Rh.2.289S., D.S.18.64, Ph.1.180, Ep.Hebr.11.23, Plu.Pomp.6, IG22.1077.34; ib.12.173.10; = Lat. edictum, OGI458.81 , BGU1074.3 , etc.; = Lat. formula, IG14.951.24,25 ; testamentary disposition, P…

διαταλαντόομαι.definition: Pass., swing to and fro, of a ship, Ach.Tat.3.1

διαταμιεύω.definition: manage, dispense, Pl.Lg.805e:—Med., store, husband, Id.Criti.111d

διατάμνω.definition: Ion. and Dor. for Hdt.2.139, Tab.Heracl.1.12

διαταράσσω.definition: Att. throw into confusion, X.Mem.4.2.40, Pl.Lg.693c, Plb.11.1.9, Phld.Piet.108:—Pass., Isoc.2.39, cf. Epicur.Ep.3p.66U., D.S.18.7, Jul.Or.3.116d

διατάσσω.definition: Att. pf. BGU1151.6 (i; Med., make testamentary dispositions, Plu.2.1129a; order by will, c. inf., AP11.133 ; bequeath, BGU1151.6 :—Pass., to be bequeathed, PFay.97.13

διαταφρεύω.definition: cut off or fortify by a ditch, Plb.3.105.11, Plu.Pomp.62:—Pass., J.BJ5.4.2

διατείνω.definition: stretch to the uttermost; intr., extend, Diog.Apoll.6; Arist.EN1172a23; Id.HA503b21; . . Plb.3.37.9; to continue, Plu.Marc.30

διατειχίζω.definition: cut off and fortify by a wall, Ar.Eq.818; divide as by a wall, X.Smp.5.6: metaph., keep apart, Ph.1.632, al.; is separated from it, Luc.Hist.Conscr.7

διατείχισμα.definition: place walled off and fortified; wall between two places, SIG421.46 , Plb.8.34.9: metaph., wall of partition, Luc.DMeretr.11.4

διατήρησις.definition: preservation, LXXEx.16.33,al.; D.S.2.50; Ph.1.203; J.AJ1.3.2, etc

διατίθημι.definition: manage well or ill, usu. with Adv., Th.6.15; D.19.88; of persons, treat himself barbarously, Hdt.3.155:—Pass., he was not very gently handled, Th.6.57; reduced to helplessness, Lys.18.23; Pl.Criti.121b; Men.591

διατίμησις.definition: valuation, Ath.6.274e, cf. D.S.29.10, POxy.267.18 ; assessed value, PRev.Laws 55.24

διατιτρώσκω.definition: pierce through, transfix, Hp.Fract.11; D.C.63.3:—Pass., J.BJ6.3.1

διατμίζω.definition: evaporate, Arist.Mete.344b23,353b8, Sor.1.106, Corn.ND32, etc.: c. acc. cogn., Plu.2.695c:—Pass., in same sense, Arist.Cael.305b14; of perspiration, Aret.CA1.1

διατονόομαι.definition: to be in a state of tension, Pall.Febr.12

διατοξεύσιμος.definition: that can be shot across, a place within bowshot, Plu.Luc.28

διατοξεύω.definition: shoot through: metaph., shoot; Med., contend with others in archery, X.Cyr.1.4.4; Parth.4.4

διατορεύω.definition: engrave, chase, S.Fr.315; Aristeas79; Ph.1.105; Plu.2.1083e:—Pass., Ael.VH14.7, Hierocl.p.37A

διατορέω.definition: strike through, pierce, Anon. ap. Suid

διατραγῳδέω.definition: = interpol. in D.18.22; also gloss on Hsch

διατραχηλίζομαι.definition: put one's neck under the yoke; fall head over heels, Plu.2.501e

διατρίζω.definition: pf. squeak, creak, Agath.5.7: c. acc. cogn., prob. in Plu.2.994e

διατρώγω.definition: fut. Ar.V.164: aor; c. gen. rei, eat of, Ael.VH1.10

διαττάω.definition: sift, riddle, Hp.Ulc.21, Pl.Sph.226b, al., SIG2587.60, Ruf. ap. Orib.7.26.97:—Pass., Pl.Cra.402c, IG22.463.83, Thphr.HP3.18.5. .)

διατυγχάνω.definition: go wrong, make a mistake, PMasp.76.15

διατυπόω.definition: form, D.S.3.67; give; metaph., imagine, conceive, Act., Luc.Alex.4; Chor.p.213 B., cf. Hdn.4.3.8; represent, portray, Plu.2.83a; Lib.Eth.27.2

διαυγάζω.definition: glance, shine through; = Hsch.: and so metaph., being enlightened, perceiving the truth, J.AJ5.10.4

διαύγεια.definition: = foreg., Philostr.Im.2.1; translucency, Plu.2.914b, Hierocl.CA26p.480M.: metaph. of sayings, clarity, Plu.2.408e

διαυγής.definition: translucent, of water, Arist.Mir.840b34, AP9.227 , 277 : Sup., v.l. in Arist.Mu.397a16; Alex.Aphr.Pr.1.68, cf. Ecphant. ap. Stob.4.7.64; radiant, of metal, Call.Lav.Pall.21; of stars, A.R.2.1104; of gems, AP5.204; Ari…

διαυλία.definition: duet on the flute, Hsch., EM269.30

διαύλιον.definition: an air on the flute in the interval of the choral song, Sch.Ar.Ra.1282, Hsch.: Suid

διαυλοδρομέω.definition: to run the Sch.Ar.Av.293; return to the starting-point, Arist.GA741b21; of the moon, Ph.1.24; of evils, recur, Id.2.350

διαυλωνισμός.definition: passage of wind through a narrow opening, Eust.1107.63

διαφαιρέω.definition: take quite away: aor. Med. v.l. in Paul. Aeg.6.35, Prob.l. in LXX1 Ki.17.39

διαφαρμακεύω.definition: give medicine to, v.l. in Plu.2.157c

διαφαυλίζω.definition: hold cheap, depreciate, Pl.Lg.804b, Hierocl.p.59A., Lib.Decl.50.48

διαφέρω.definition: fut. S.OT321, h.Merc.255; of Time, go through life, Hdt.3.40, E.Hel.[10]; Id.Rh.600: abs., ib.982:—Med., live, continue, Hp.Art.56; will pass his life apart from thee, S.Aj.511; X.Mem.2.1.24

διαφεύγω.definition: fut. Pl.Prm.135d:—get away from; escape one's notice or memory, Pl.Phd.95e, Men.96e; Id.Prm.135d; Jul.Or.7.228a; Isoc.4.187

διάφευξις.definition: escaping, means of escape, Th.3.23, J.AJ17.10.7, Plu.TG5 , D.C.40.32; avoidance, Phld.Rh.1.192S

διαφημίζω.definition: make known, spread abroad, D.H.11.46; call, name, Arat.221:—Med., Id.442 , D.P.50

διαφθορά.definition: Ion. destruction, ruin, Th.8.86; Hdt.4.164; Pl.Mx.242d: pl., S.OT573, etc. 2. destruction, blight, of things, Id.OC552; A.Pr.643. 3. in moral sense, corruption, seduction, X.Ap.19; Arist.Rh.1372a34 . 4. miscarriage, a…

διαφθορεύς.definition: corrupter, Pl.Cri.53c; Them.Or.23.296b: as fem., E.Hipp.682

διαφίημι.definition: aor. X. and Plb. : inf. D.23.171: fut. is f.l. in Th.7.32: dismiss, disband, X.HG3.2.24; D.l.c.; an assembly, Plb.3.63.14,al

διαφιλοτιμέομαι.definition: strive emulously or earnestly, Thphr.HP4.4.1; Plu.Arist.16

διαφλέγω.definition: burn up, LXXPs.82.15:—Pass., Plu.Alc.39: metaph., inflame, Id.Mar.16; Heraclit.All.20

διαφλύω.definition: in Pass., to be permeated, Hp.Mul.1.77

διαφορέω.definition: = spread abroad, disperse; plunder, Plu.Brut.6, etc.:—Med., PSI5.522.5 :—most freq. in Pass., Hdt.3.53; D.19.315; to be robbed of one's wits, Pl.Lg.672b

διαφόρησις.definition: plundering, stealing; evaporation, dissipation, Sor.1.22, Olymp.in Mete.145.14; perspiration, Cic.Fam.16.18.1; Plu.Fr. inc.149

διαφόρητος.definition: torn in pieces, prob. in E.Cyc.344

διάφορος.definition: different, unlike, Hdt.2.83, 4.81; several, various, Phld.Sign.24; POxy.1033.88 , cf. Ep.Hebr.9.13

διαφράσσω.definition: Att. = IG12.373.251; ib.2.1054.63, cf. D.S.17.96, Them.Or.20.235d:—Pass., to be divided off, Dsc.2.24; Erasistr. ap. Gal.5.603, cf. Hdn.3.1.4; obstructed, Ruf.Anat.30; but with divisions, Thphr.HP8.5.2

διάφρυκτος.definition: parched, of beans used in voting, Hsch.:—hence vote or cast lots, Id., EM271.50, Suid

διαφυλάσσω.definition: observe closely; observe, maintain, Pl.Lg.951b, cf. SIG1044.10 , PTeb.25.3 ; Philipp. ap. D.18.78; Plb.1.78.8; IG12.241.22 ; guard against being too particular . ., Pl.Plt.261e; take care that . ., Id.Criti.112d

διαφύομαι.definition: Pass., fut. Philostr.Jun.Im.13; to be disjoined, Emp.17.10

διαφυσικεύομαι.definition: study natural philosophy, Julian. ap. Gal.18.256

διαφωνέω.definition: to be a discord, in Music; generally, disagree, Id.Lg.860a, etc.; Arist.Metaph.1085b36; there is a discrepancy in the accounts, Plb.21.43.23; Pl.Plt.292b, etc.; Id.Phd.101d; Arist.EN1098b12,al.; Iamb.Myst.9.3:—Pass., …

διαφωνία.definition: discord, disagreement, Pl.Lg.689a, 691a, Str.2.1.7, Plu.2.861a, etc.; inconsistency, Phld.Po.994.4; esp. in Music, discord, Bacch.Harm.59, prob. in Cleonid.Harm.5

διάφωνος.definition: discordant, inconsistent, D.S.4.55, cf. Plu.2.1039d, etc.; with one, Luc.Cyn.16; esp. in Music, strike a false note, Damox.2.61, cf. Hp.Vict.1.18 , etc.; opp. Euc.Sect.Can.Praef., Theo Sm.p.49H. Adv. Plu.2.1137c: c.da…

διαφωτίζω.definition: enlighten, Plu.2.76b; clear a place by force, Id.Cat.Ma.20; throw light upon, Luc.Icar.21: abs., dawn, LXXNe.8.3

διαχαράσσω.definition: Att. sever, divide, D.H.Dem.43 ; strip off, Agath.4.23; carve, give shape to, Plu.2.636c , cf. Ph.1.649 ; sharpen, Plu.2.974b:—Med., scrape, S.Ichn.255:—Pass., Agath.4.20

διαχάσκω.definition: aor. 2 pf. yawn, Ar.Eq.533, Thphr.HP3.9.1, Plu.2.976b, 980b; Agath.2.32, 5.3

διαχειρίζω.definition: have in hand, conduct, manage; Med., lay hands on, slay, Plb.8.21.8, Act.Ap.5.30, Plu.2.220b, D.C.72.14

διαχειριστικόν.definition: commission paid for handling grain, PLond.ined.2093

διαχειροτονέω.definition: choose between two persons or proposals; vote on a person's case, Arist.Ath.49.2

διαχειροτονία.definition: choice between two persons or things, election, = D.24.25, IG12.237.19 ; to allow a right of election, Aeschin.3.39

διαχλευάζω.definition: strengthd. for c.acc., D.50.49; deceive, Gp.7.7.5

διαχράομαι.definition: Dep., c. dat. rei, use constantly or habitually, chiefly in Hdt., 1.58; 2.127; 1.71, cf. 2.77; 4.43; speak the truth, 3.72; 3.66, cf. 6.58; 7.102; 6.10; 7.210; Ar.Ec.609; use hunger as a sauce, X.Cyr.1.5.12

διάχριστος.definition: anointed: hence a rich cake, Lynceus ap.Ath.3.109e: salves, ointments, Dsc.1.30, Antyll. ap. Orib.10.34 tit., Aret.CA1.1

διαχυλόομαι.definition: to be made into a syrup, Hippiatr.32

διαχωρέω.definition: pass through, Pl.Ti.78a, PFlor.200.4 (iii; abscond, PSI4.359.7

διαχώρησις.definition: excretion, Hp.Aph.2.18, Arist.PA675a22, Phld.D.3.14 , Porph.Abst.1.45; Hp.Aph.5.64

διαχωρίζω.definition: separate, X.Oec.9.7; Pl.Plt.262b; Epicr.11.14:—Med., Ar.Th.14:—Pass., Pl.Ti.59c, Phlb.17a; divorced, J.AJ15.7.10

διαψαθάλλω.definition: feel with the fingers, scratch, Hsch

διαψεύδω.definition: deceive, D.Ep.3.34:—Med., abs., And.1.42: c; Med., deny, disclaim, A.D.Synt.115.24, Pron.81.17

διαψηλαφάω.definition: handle a thing, Herod. Med. ap. Orib.6.20.10, Sor.1.100, Aq.Ge.31.34, Sm.Is.59.10

διαψηφίζω.definition: Dor. aor. inf. put to the; more freq. Dep. Att. fut. vote by ballot, Antipho5.8, Hyp.Eux.40, etc.; Pl.Lg.937a; And.4.3, Th.4.88

διαψήφισις.definition: voting by ballot, Pl.Lg.855d; esp. of a vote on claims to registration of citizens, Aeschin.1.77, D.57.26 ; X.HG1.7.14; of a criminal confessing his guilt, Lys.12.34

διαψηφισμός.definition: = foreg., Arist.Ath.13.5, Ath.5.218a; reckoning, assessment, IG5.1432

διαψηφοφορέομαι.definition: of candidates for office, to be submitted to a ballot, Ath.Mitt.32.294

διαψιθυρίζω.definition: whisper among themselves, LXXSi.12.18, Plb.15.26.8, Luc.Gall.25

διαψύχω.definition: cool, Hp.VM16:—Pass., to be chilly; air, dry and clean, Th.7.12, cf. Luc.Cont.23, etc.: metaph. of misers bringing out their hoards, X.Cyr.8.2.21

διδακτυλιαῖος.definition: two fingers long or broad, S.E.M.10.156, cf. Heliod. ap. Orib.48.23.2, etc.:—so Hp.Art.7, Thphr.HP9.5.3, IG22.463.78

διδασκάλιον.definition: thing taught, science or art (=; in pl., = Plu.Lyc.14, Alex.7, al

διδράσκω.definition: run away, Hsch.: pf., Eun.Hist.p.255 D.: aor. imper. prob. l. in Tab.Defix.Aud.26 ; part. POxy.1423.6 ; but mostly found in compds., esp

διδυμόχροος.definition: two-coloured, Musae.59: heterocl. dat. sg. Nonn.D.11.378, acc. pl. ib.21.216

διεγγυάω.definition: give bail to produce, D.H.7.12:—Med., to take bail for, Isoc.17.14, cf. Plu.Caes.11:—Pass., to be bailed by any one, bailed by their Proxeni for eight hundred talents, Th.3.70

διεγείρω.definition: wake up, Anaxipp.1.47, J.AJ8.13.7; raise, Hld.4.4; J.BJ6.1.1, 6.2.7:—Pass., LXXJu.1.4; p.137B

διεικάζομαι.definition: Pass., pf. inf. to be like, c. dat., Philostr.Im.1.19

διεκβολή.definition: mountain-pass, in pl., Plb.1.75.4; estuary, Str.9.5.22

διεκδύομαι.definition: aor. , slip out through, Hp.Morb.Sacr.7; Plu.Tim.10: abs., prob. in Id.Pel.17

διεκπαίω.definition: break or burst through, J.BJ5.2.2, cf. Philostr.Her.19.4, Im.2.23; Paus.7.16.5: c. acc., Diox.3, cf. App.BC5.34, etc.: abs., Luc.Tox.61:—Med., D.H.11.37; Plu.Sert.21: abs., J.BJ7.6.4, Polyaen.4.2.14; Iamb.VP35.249

διεκπορεύομαι.definition: go out through, D.H.9.26; pass through, traverse, M.Ant.7.19

διεκτετραίνω.definition: gloss on Hsch.; v.l. for Heliod. ap. Orib.49.23.15

διεκτρέχω.definition: aor. traverse, Ph.Bel.77.36; . . . . Orph.Fr.285.5: abs., sally, rush out, J.AJ5.2.11; Plu.2.490d

διελέγχω.definition: refute, Pl.Grg.457e, Arist.Fr.94, Plb.7.3.3; convict, expose, Ph.1.265, al., Plu.2.437b, PLips.40iii23 :—Pass., Philostr.Jun.Im.1, BGU321.14

διεμβάλλω.definition: put in through, LXXNu.4.6, al., Gal.2.574, Aët.15.12

διεμφανίζω.definition: let a thing be seen, Aristaenet.2.16

διενιαυτίζω.definition: live out the year, Hdt.4.7; spend a whole year, POxy.899.11

διενοχλέω.definition: annoy, Ph.2.590, J.AJ9.3.1 , Aristaenet.1.5: abs., Luc.Symp.14:—Pass., BGU830.8

διεξαγωγή.definition: settlement of a dispute, Plb.5.102.3; inquiry, inquest, PTeb.14.6 , PRyl.65.10

διεξελαύνω.definition: Att. fut. intr., drive, ride, march through, abs., Hdt.1.187: c. acc. loci, Id.3.11; Id.5.52, etc.; also Id.3.86; Id.7.100; Plu.Publ.19: c. gen. loci, Id.Cam.7

διεξελέγχω.definition: refute utterly, Luc.Alex.61, Plu.2.922e, Gal.4.518:—Pass., when they are convicted of ignorance, Them.Or.21.259b

διεξεργάζομαι.definition: work out, effect, Pl.Lg.798d; make away with, v.l. in and D.H.6.35

διεξερευνάω.definition: examine or survey closely, Pi.N.3.24 :—Med., Pl.Lg.763a, cf. Phlb.58d

διεξέρχομαι.definition: folld. by go through in succession, i. e. killing them one after another, Id.3.11; Pl.Prt.315a

διεξιππάζομαι.definition: ride out through, dub. for , Polyaen.5.16.5

διέξοδος.definition: outlet, passage, Hp.Aph.7.51; pathway, orbit, of the sun, Hdt.2.24; three days, E.Andr.1086; of planets, Arist.Mu.399a3: metaph., Henioch.4.5; the paths of his counsels, Hdt.3.156; Ocell.1.5, 12; Plot.6.7.13

διεορτάζω.definition: keep the feast throughout, Th.8.9, cf. Plu.Pyrrh.20: plpf. D.C.47.20:—Pass., these festivities were kept, Id.51.21

διέραμα.definition: funnel, strainer, Plu.2.1088e; hopper for lading corn in bulk, PThead.26, 27 : hence, contractor for use of II, POxy.1197.4

διεργάζομαι.definition: work thoroughly, cultivate, but pf. part; work out, Isoc.10.69; Plb.3.73.7

διερεθισμός.definition: provocation, Phld.Ir.p.26 W.: pl., ib.p.29 W.; irritation, Paul.Aeg.3.66

διερείδω.definition: prop up, Plu.2.529c, Luc.VH2.1; hold apart, as the collar-bones do the shoulders, Sor.2.63: so metaph., of vowels, thrust apart, D.H.Comp.22

διέρεισμα.definition: supporting beam, IG2.1054.68, 11.287 A84 ; also ib.2.652A25

διερευνάω.definition: track down, Pl.Sph.241b; search, examine, CPHerm. 8ii5 , Jul.Or.7.222c, etc.:—freq. in Med., Pl.Phd.78a, Mx.240b, Onos.6.7, Plu.Them.10, etc.; Pl.R.368c:— Pass., Plb.14.2.1

διερεύνησις.definition: investigation, Str.16.4.5, Iamb.Comm.Math.22, dub. in Epicur.Nat.135 G

διερμηνεύω.definition: interpret, expound, Plb.3.22.3, Epicur.Nat.1431.17, Phld.Rh.1.84S., 1 Ep.Cor.14.27; translate, Aristeas15:—Pass., LXX2 Ma.1.36, PTaur.1v4, Ph.1.226

διέρομαι.definition: Ep. ask or question closely, Od.4.492; Il.1.550, etc.: aor. inf., Pl.Phlb.42e; D.C.38.4

διερπύζω.definition: = sq., c. acc., Opp.H.2.261, Hld.6.1: c. gen., Nonn.D.13.565, al

διερωτάω.definition: cross-question, Pl.Ap.22b, Grg.458a; ask constantly or continually, . . D.3.22

διετηρίς.definition: space of two years, LXX2 Ki.13.23, IGRom.4.850

διετήσιος.definition: lasting through the year, Th.2.38, cf. Inscr.Prien.112.69 . Adv. Ar.Fr.766

διευεργετέω.definition: to be a firm friend to, Sch.A.Pers.854

διευκρινέω.definition: pf. Phld.Rh.2.47 S. :—arrange; examine thoroughly, elucidate, Plb.2.56.4; . . Id.3.28.5; D.H.Comp.20, cf. Phld.l.c., Porph.Abst.2.4, etc.:—Pass., Plb.6.5.1, cf. Iamb.Myst.8.4, al.:—Att., only in Med., as Pl.Prm.135b, …

διευκρίνησις.definition: analysis, discussion, elucidation, Ptol.Alm.12.3, Simp.in Cael.194.2

διευλυτέω.definition: pay off, liquidate debts, etc., BGU1151.42 , J.AJ16.9.3:—Pass., POxy.268.15

διευλυτόω.definition: = pay off a debt, PTeb.381.18; clear themselves from charges, Just.Nov.123.22

διευλύτωσις.definition: discharge of a debt, Gloss., prob. in Petersen-Luschan Reisen in Lykienp.12 No.19

διευριπιδίζω.definition: play the part of Euripides, Sch.Ar.Eq.19

διευρύνω.definition: dilate, in Pass., Hp.Morb.4.52, Aen.Tact.31.12, Arist.de An.422a3

διευτυχέω.definition: continue prosperous, D.42.4; Ael.NA17.27; Theopomp.Hist.111: abs., Men.531.3, etc.; fare thee well, CIG4076 , cf. PMag.Berol.1.194, BGU 1197.23

διεφικνέομαι.definition: pf. dub. sens. in Eun.Hist.p.361 D

διέχεια.definition: breach of continuity, Aristid.Quint.3.10, Sch.Ar.Pax938; to be reckoned exclusively, Steph.in Hp.1.198 D

διεχθρεύω.definition: strengthd. for D.H.4.70, Arr.Cyn.12.5; enmity, Alciphr.2.3

διηγέομαι.definition: set out in detail, describe, Heraclit.1; Ar.Av.198; Antipho1.13, cf. Th.6.54, Pl.Prt.310a, al.; D.21.77: c. acc. pers., . . such as you describe him, Pl.Tht.144c

διήγημα.definition: tale, Phoenicid.4.15; Plb.1.14.6, cf. LXXDe.28.37, Polem.Call.42, Porph.Antr.4, etc

διήγησις.definition: narration, narrative, Pl.R.392d, Phdr.246a, Aristeas1, Ev.Luc.1.1, etc.; in a speech, statement of the case, Arist.Rh.1416b29, Zeno Stoic.1.23

διήθησις.definition: straining, percolation, Epicur.Ep.2p.45U., Thphr.CP6.1.1, Plu.Ant.3: pl., D.Chr.33.6; filtering of urine in kidneys, Aret.SD2.3; haemorrhage, Aët.15.10

διθυραμβοδιδάσκαλος.definition: dithyrambic poet who trained his own chorus, Ar.Pax829

διϊκνέομαι.definition: fut. aor. through; of Time, intervene, Longus1.4

διίπταμαι.definition: late pres., = Arist.Mir.839a23, Hdn.2.8.7, Luc.Am.6, Max.Tyr.22.6; impf. J.BJ3.7.20

διΐστημι.definition: fut. set apart, separate; set one at variance with another, Ar.V.41, Th.6.77; divide it into factions, Hdt.9.2; D.H.9.17

διϊσχυριείω.definition: wish or mean to affirm, Hp.Art.1

διϊσχυρίζομαι.definition: lean upon, rely on; affirm confidently, Pl.Phd.63c, etc.; ib.114d; . . Id.Tht.154a; And.2.4, Lys.13.85; Pl.Men.86b; . . Id.Ep.317c: abs., Id.Tht.158d, etc

δικαιοθέτης.definition: = foreg., Baillet Inscr.des tombeaux des rois 1836

δικαιοπραγέω.definition: act honestly, Arist.EN1135a16, PTeb.183 , Ceb.41, Plu.Sol.5, Sallust.19, etc.; Jason ap.Plu.2.135f; Arist.Rh.1373b22

δικαιοπράγημα.definition: just or righteous act, Id.EN1135a12, Chrysipp.Stoic.3.73

δικαιοπραγής.definition: acting justly, PSI1.76.5 , Sch.Ar.Av.1354, Suid. s.v

δικαιοπραγία.definition: just or righteous dealing, Arist.EN1133b30, Phld.Rh.1.266S., Porph.Marc.11, Jul.Ep.89; title of work by Epicurus

δικαιοσύνη.definition: righteousness, justice, Thgn.147; fulfilment of the Law, LXXIs.26.2, al., Ev.Matt.3.15, al

δικαιόσυνος.definition: Guardian of justice, of Zeus, AJA1905.302 , Com.Adesp.752, Eust.918.47: generally, just, Simp.in Cat.264.24

δικαιοφανής.definition: having an appearance of justice, Sch.Th.6.80

δίκασις.definition: exercise of the function of a Sch.Ar.Pl.277

δικασταγωγός.definition: official who escorted foreign to their homes, Milet.3.152.94 ; IG5.39

δικαστής.definition: a judge, Hdt.1.96, 3.14,31; at Athens and elsewh., juror, S.Aj.1136, etc.; opp. Lys.14.4, cf. Antipho1.23, X.Smp.5.10

δικαστοφιλακέω.definition: to be a member of the bodyguard of a jury, Inscr. Magn.93a.23

δίκελλα.definition: two-pronged fork, Ps.-Phoc.158, A.Fr.196, S.Ant.250, E.Ph.1155, IG11.159A57 , etc.; Men.Georg.65

δικέντητον.definition: name of an eyesalve, Dem. Ophth. ap. Aët.7.117

δικέρως.definition: two-horned, h.Hom.19.2, AP6.32 , etc.: also Orph.Fr.274, Arist.HA499b18

δικογράφος.definition: composer of forensic speeches, Hyp.Fr.234, D.L.6.15

δικολόγος.definition: pleader, advocate, Plu.Luc.1, Ptol.Tetr.180, Edict.Diocl.7.72, PFlor.71.692 , Artem.2.29

δικόνδυλος.definition: double-knuckled; provided with two knobs , Sammelb.1958

δίκορος.definition: having a double pupil, Ptol.Chenn.p.192W., Suid., Eust.295.44

δικορραφέω.definition: stitch, i. e. get up, a lawsuit, Ar.Nu.1483, Apollod.Com.13.12

δικορραφία.definition: getting up a lawsuit, Man.2.296, Sch.Ar.Nu.1015

δικόρυμβος.definition: twin-peaked, of Parnassus, Pae.Delph.4, cf. Luc.Cont.5

δικόρυφος.definition: two-peaked, of Parnassus; with two crowns, of the hair on the head, Arist.HA491b7, Poll.2.43

δικραιόομαι.definition: branch, fork, prob. in Hp.Epid.2.4.1 ; cf. Erot

δίκροος.definition: contr. or contr. also written cloven, A.Fr.152, cf. X.Cyn.10.7; Timocl.9.6; Arist.HA590b25, etc.; of a serpent's tongue, Id.PA660b6, al.; of the womb, in selachians, Id.HA511a6; of muscles and tendons, Gal.2.369; Thph…

δίκροτος.definition: double-beating, E.IT408; of ships, with only two banks of oars manned, X.HG2.1.28; later, = Arr.An.6.5.2, Luc.Am.6: Subst. Plb.5.62.3, App.Mith.17; AP7.640

δικτυοειδής.definition: net-like, rete mirabile Galeni, Herophil. ap. Gal.5.155, Gal.UP9.4

δικτυόκλωστος.definition: woven in meshes, the net's meshy coils, S.Ant.347

δικτυόομαι.definition: Pass., to be wrought in net-work, LXX3; to be caught in a net, Babr.107.11

δίκωλος.definition: with two limbs or legs, Lyc.636; in Rhet., with two members, Demetr.Eloc.34, Hermog.Inv.4.3, Hdn.Fig.p.98S.:—also in metre, Sch.Ar.Ach.1212, etc

δίλογχος.definition: double-pointed, twofold, A.Ag.643; epith. of from her twofold attributes, Cratin.80

διμερής.definition: bipartite, of the human body, the brain, etc., Arist.PA667b32, al.; Ph.1.523; J.AJ12.2.12; Jul.Or.6.190a. Adv. in two instalments, Jahresh. 18 Beibl.23

διμηνιαῖος.definition: two months old, Hp.Nat.Mul.19, Mul.1.47; of two months, Cleom.1.7, Gem.6.14, Gp.17.3.3

διμήτωρ.definition: Dor. twice-born, of Bacchus, Alex.283, Orph.H.52.9, D.S.3.62:—also Et.Gud., Hdn.Epim.265

διμναῖος.definition: Ion. worth or costing two minae, to value at two minae, Hdt.5.77; Arist.Oec.1347a23; Luc.DMeretr.14.4:—also Ph.Bel.69.13: Subst. weight of two minae, IG22.1013.55

διμοιρία.definition: double share, X.An.7.2.36, Lac.15.4; two-thirds, D.H.8.77, BGU136.8

δίμυξος.definition: with two wicks, Philyll.26, Philonid.4, Pl.Com.84, Metagen.12, CIG3071.9

Διόβολος.definition: = foreg.I, of the thunderbolt, S.OC1464 , E.Alc.128

Διογενέτωρ.definition: giving birth to Zeus, natal cave of Zeus, E.Ba.122

διοίκημα.definition: sum of money administered, Hsch., Suid. s.v

διοικονομέω.definition: strengthd. for Phld.Oec.p.9J. , Anon.Lond.22.49, Poll.5.156:—Pass., Arist.Mu.400b32

διοίχομαι.definition: fut. pf. Hdt.4.136:—to; to be gone through, ended, S.OC574 ; E.Supp.530

διόμνυμι.definition: or ), swear solemnly, declare on oath, esp. in courts of justice, c. fut. inf., . . S.Tr.255; Lycurg.127:—more freq. in Med., fut. aor. vow, asseverate, S.Aj.1233, Tr.378: c. inf., Plu.Num.2; Id.Cam.39: esp. of the , …

Διονυσαλέξανδρος.definition: Dionysus masquerading as Paris, title of play by Cratinus, POxy.663, etc

Διονύσιον.definition: the temple of Dionysus, Th.8.93, Ar.Fr.131, Paus.1.43.5, etc

Διονύσιος.definition: name of month in Aetolia, IG9.374, cf. SIG524.14 , 1009.20 , etc

Διονυσοδότης.definition: bestower of Dionysus, Olymp.in Phd.p.111 N

Διονυσομανέω.definition: to be full of Bacchic frenzy, Philostr.VA5.32

Διονυσοπλάτων.definition: double herm of Dionysus and Plato as a signet, POxy.105.20

διοπτρισμός.definition: use of the speculum, Sor.2.40, Paul.Aeg.6.73

διοργανόομαι.definition: to be provided with organs, Iamb.VP15.66; of the foetus, Agath.4.25

διοργάνωσις.definition: formation, fashioning, Iamb.VP15.67; structural differentiation, Procl.in Prm.p.616 S., Simp.in Cael.389.19

διοργίζομαι.definition: to be very angry, Plb.2.8.13; LXX3 Ma.3.1 , Plu.Ages.6; Phld.Ir.p.9 W.; D.S.14.14

διοργυιόομαι.definition: stretch out the arms: with arms akimbo, Hipparch.1.7.22: metaph., Dam.Pr.123 bis

διορθρίζω.definition: rise early, v.l. in LXX1 Ki.29.10

διόρθωμα.definition: making straight, setting right; amendment, Plu.Num.17; revision, PRev.Laws 57.1

διορθωτής.definition: a corrector, LXXWi.7.15; esp. of books, editor, reviser, D.S.15.6, Gal.8.758

διορκίζω.definition: adjure, Sammelb.4324.13:—Pass., of an oath, to be sworn, dub. in Wilcken Chr.110 A 27

διορμάομαι.definition: to be impelled, c. inf., Max.Tyr.41.5

διορύσσω.definition: Att. dig through; metaph., undermine, ruin, D.45.30; Lib.Or.1.123; Id.Decl.1.41:—Pass., Plu.Phoc.12, cf. Him.Ecl.5.6

διορυχή.definition: = D.7.40; Ph.1.626; Lib.Decl.8.19: metaph., undermining, Id.Or.63.21

Διοσημία.definition: a sign from Zeus, an omen from the sky, esp. of thunder, lightning, rain, Ar.Ach.171: pl., Stoic.2.203, D.S.2.19, Plu.2.419e, Philostr.VA2.33, Jul.Or.7.212b

διοσκέω.definition: look earnestly at, Anacr.3; also expld. by Hsch

Διοσκόρειον.definition: temple of the Dioscuri, Th.4.110; festival of the Dioscuri, IG5.559 : SIG2438.175 : SIG1067.15

Διοσκόριος.definition: name of a month in Syria, cj. in LXX2 Ma.11.21; in Crete, Hemerolog.Flor

διοσφραίνω.definition: give a smell to, perfume, Sch.Ar.Ra.1107

Διοτρεφής.definition: fostered, cherished by Zeus, Il.2.196, Hes.Th.82, etc.; Il.2.660; also of the Scamander, fed by rain, 21.223

διοχετεύω.definition: furnish with channels, Pl.Ti.77c; distribute by conduits, Luc.VH1.33:—Pass., D.S.20.8: metaph. of the spinal cord, Ruf.Anat.7

διοχλέω.definition: annoy exceedingly, Lys.6.6; weary, bore, D.19.329: pf. Jul.Or.2.78b; press for payment, POxy.286.13 ; later, Aeschin.Ep.2.2, Plu.Cim.18, Longus3.20: abs., Ph.1.356:—Pass., Luc.Am.50, IG3.48 ; D.H.Comp.11

διπάλαιστος.definition: two palms broad or long, X.Cyn.2.4, Plb.27.11.2:—also Heliod. ap. Orib.49.8.6, Gp.9.10.2

διπενθημιμερής.definition: consisting of two members of 2 1/2 feet , Heph.15.10; Sch.Ar.Pax775:—also Sacerd.p.512 K

διπλασιάζω.definition: double, Pl.Lg.920a, Hierocl.in; Gramm., reduplicate, A.D.Pron.62.23, al.:—Pass., Id.Synt.237.23

διπλασιασμός.definition: doubling, Antipho Soph.75; Gramm., the Ionic doubling of consonants, as in EM68.47, Eust.73.3, etc

διπλασιεπιδίμοιρος.definition: Gaud.Harm.10, and Nicom.Ar.1.23, 2 2/3 times as great

διπλασιεπιδίτριτος.definition: ibid., Domnin. in Rev.Phil.7.90, 2 2/3 times as great

διπλασιεπιτετραμερής.definition: ib.23, and ibid., 2 4/5 times as great

διπλασιεπίτριτος.definition: ib.22, Theo Sm.p.110H., 2 1/3 times as great

διπλασιόομαι.definition: Pass., to be doubled, Th.1.69, PLeid.X.87

διπλασιόπλευρος.definition: with two sides twice as long as the other two, Arist.Mech.856a39

διπλάσιος.definition: Subst. as much again, Hdt.7.103: as Adv., Thgn.229; Adv. Th.8.1, Men.645; Aeschin.2.122, AP7.611

διπλασίων.definition: gen. later form for Arist.Pr.923a3, Mu.399a9, Arr.Tact.16.11, PLips.64.31 , etc.; duplicate ratio, Ph.1.22, Plu.2.1138e

διπλοκάριος.definition: = Lat. duplicarius, receiving double pay, PGrenf.2.51.5

διπλοκεράμιον.definition: measure of wine in Egypt, Ostr. 1166, al., POxy.1751.3

δίπνοος.definition: with two breathing apertures, Gal.19.93 ; cf. Hsch

διπτέρυγος.definition: = foreg. I, AP5.150 , cf; mantle with two , IG2.754.38, Jahresh.16 Beibl.53

διπτυχίζω.definition: Dor. aor. imper. fold, double, Hsch

δίσημος.definition: of doubtful quantity, Sch.D.T.p.38H; in Rhythm, of two time-units, Aristox.Rhyth.2.10,31, cf. Aristid.Quint.1.14

δίστεγος.definition: of two stories, Sammelb; of two chambers on the same floor, J.BJ5.5.4

διστιχία.definition: double row or line, of fruit, J.AJ8.3.4; couplet, distich, Heph.Poëm.1, Sch.Ar.Nu.1348

διστιχίασις.definition: = II, Sever. ap. Aët.7.68, Paul. Aeg.6.8

δίστοιχος.definition: in two rows, Arist.HA501a24; ib.505a16; two-rowed barley, Thphr.HP8.4.2; in two courses, SIG 969.32

δισυλλαβέω.definition: to be of two syllables, Hdn Gr.2.908, A.D.Pron.78.24
