δισώματος.definition: double-bodied, D.S.4.12, Orph.H.71.5, Fr.57, Ph.2.481; with two chambers, CIG2842

διτάλαντος.definition: weighing two talents, Hdt.1.50, 2.96; worth two talents, D.18.312; Id.27.64: neut. as Subst., LXX4 Ki.5.23

διτορμία.definition: double socket or tenon, Ph.Bel.63.24, HeroBel.92.9, Spir.1.42

διυγιαίνω.definition: to be healthy throughout, Plu.2.135c, Iamb.VP22.102

διυφαίνω.definition: fill up by weaving; interweave, in Pass., Ael.NA9.17; Aristeas97, cf. LXXEx.36.31

διφαλαγγαρχία.definition: corps of two or 8,192 men , Ael.Tact.9.9, Arr.Tact.10.7

διφθεράλοιφος.definition: Cypr. for a schoolmaster, JHS12.330, Hsch

διφθερίας.definition: clad in a leathern jerkin; the dress of old men in Tragedy, of boors in Comedy, Posidipp. ap. Ath.10.414e, Luc.Tim.8, Poll.4.137

διφθογγόομαι.definition: to be written with a diphthong, Hdn.Epim.276

διφορέω.definition: to bear double, esp. of fruit; Pass., to be spelt or pronounced in two ways, Hdn.Gr.2.543, EM197. 51, al

διχηλέω.definition: divide the hoof, Arist.PA695a18 , Aristeas150, LXXLe.11.3, al., Ph.2.353

δίχηλος.definition: cloven-hoofed, Hdt.2.71; with two pincers, prongs, or claws, AP6.92 ; ib.196 , cf. HeroBel.76.10; BGU 37.4 ; HeroSpir.1.28

διχογνωμονέω.definition: to differ in opinion, X.Mem.2.6.21; doubt, Lib.Decl.43.43

διχογνώμων.definition: gen. divided between two opinions, Plu.2.11c. Adv. Poll.8.154

διχοινικία.definition: tax of two per PLond.372.25 , etc

διχοίνικος.definition: holding two Ar.Nu.640; Subst. measure of two SIG945.4

διχομηνία.definition: full moon, IG12.6.62, PRev.Laws 56.18; mid-menstrual period, Hp.Oct.13

διχομηνιαία.definition: day of full moon, Gal.9.908; also, = Lat. Idus, Suid

διχόμηνις.definition: = sq., Pi.O.3.19, cf; = Lat. Idus, D.H.1.38, etc

διχόμηνος.definition: dividing the month, i. e. at or of the full moon, h.Hom.32.11; Gp.10.48.2, cf. Plu.Flam.4; Arat.808, Ph.2.293; Gp.2.14.7, Cat.Cod.Astr.1.173

διχόμυθος.definition: double-speaking, Pittac.1 Bgk.; Sol.42.4; double-dealing, deceptive, Ant.Lib.23; speak ambiguously, E.Or.890

διχόνοια.definition: discord, disagreement, Pl.Alc.1.126c, Plu.2.70c; Ph.2.181: c. gen., disagreement with, App.BC5.33

διχορία.definition: division of a chorus into two parts, Poll.4.107, Arg.Ar.Lys.1

διχοριάζω.definition: sing in two halves, of a chorus, Hsch

διχόρροπος.definition: oscillating, Trag.Adesp.341. Adv. waveringly, doubtfully, used only by A., and always with a neg., or Ag.349, 815, 1272, Supp.605, 982

διχοστασία.definition: dissension, B.10.67 , Hdt.5.75, Eus.Mynd.45, Plu.2.20c; sedition, Sol.4.38, Thgn.78, LXX1 Ma.3.29

διχοτόμημα.definition: half of a thing cut in two: hence, generally, any portion of a thing cut up, LXXEx.29.17, Le.1.8, Ph.1.503

διχοτόμος.definition: cutting in two, Ammon.p.44V.: but; proparox., cut in half, divided equally, Arist.HA492b17; the half- moon, Id.Pr.911b36, Aristarch.Sam.Hyp.3, Gem.9.8, prob. in Plu.2.929f; Porph. ap.Eus.PE3.11; till the second quarte…

διχοφροσύνη.definition: discord, faction, ib.824d , Ocell.4.6, D.Chr.44.10, Anon. ap. Iamb.VP7.34

δίχρωμος.definition: = foreg., Luc.Prom.Es4, Gal.13.460; Subst. name of a plaster, Aët.15.13

διψάω.definition: late Ep. Tryph.548, AP11.57; metaph., thirst after a thing, Pi.N.3.6; Pl.R.562c: later c. acc., Telesp.8 H.; APl.4.137 ; Ev.Matt.5.6; J.BJ1.32.2; also LXXPs.41.2: c. dat., ib.Ex.17.3: c. inf., X.Cyr.5.1.1; Ael.VH2.41,…

διώβολον.definition: double obol, Ar.Fr.3, Alex.186, Theopomp.Com.55, Arist.Ath.41.3

διωγμός.definition: the chase, X.Cyr.1.4.21, etc; pursuit, D.S.4.13, al., Ael.Tact.34.4, Iamb.VP31.191

δογματίζω.definition: lay down as an opinion; decree by ordinance, c. inf., D.S.4.83, LXX1 Es.6.34; of the Roman Senate, J.AJ14.10.22; declare her beautiful, AP9.576 :—Pass., IG12.173.53 , cf. ib. 14.759.13

δογματογράφος.definition: drafter of decrees, IG5.26 , IGRom.4.259 , 661 , etc

δογματοποιέω.definition: make a decree, c. inf., Plb.1.81.4:— also Med., IG5.1390.57

δοκησιδέξιος.definition: clever in one's own conceit, Pherecr.154, Callias Com.27

δοκησισοφία.definition: conceit of wisdom, Pl. ap. Poll.4.9

δοκησίσοφος.definition: wise in one's own conceit, Ar.Pax44, Antipho Soph.105, Ph.1.122; ib.605

δοκιμάζω.definition: of persons, put them to the test, make trial of them, Isoc.2.50; Th.6.53; X.Mem.2.6.1, cf. PEleph.1.8 , etc.; also of Apis-bulls, Hdt.2.38

δοκιμασία.definition: examination, scrutiny; of magistrates after election, to see if they fulfil the legal requirements of legitimacy, full citizenship, etc., Lys.15.2, cf. 16.9 ; Pl.Lg.759d; Arist.Ath.59.4 , cf. IG 22.856,980

δοκιμαστέος.definition: to be approved after scrutiny; impers., one must approve after scrutiny, Lys.21.25, Epicur.Sent.Vat.28, Plu.2.3d, Max.Tyr.7.9

δοκιμαστήριον.definition: test, means of trial, Men.Mon.537, Arr.Epict.3.6.10; of the nose, Artem.4.27

δοκιμεῖον.definition: test, means of testing, Pl.Ti.65c , IG7.303.31 ; proof, OGI308.16 , cf. Zos.3.13

δοκιμόω.definition: = Parm.1.32, Pherecyd. ap. D.L.1.122, Theoc.30.25, Hsch

δοκίμωμι.definition: Aeol. form of = Sapph.69, cf. 37 , Epigr.Gr. 991.7

δοκόω.definition: furnish with rafters, in Pass., S.E.P.3.99; Sammelb.5105.3 , PGrenf.2.35

δόκωσις.definition: furnishing with rafters, roofing, LXXEc.10.18, Plu.2.1112e , S.E.P.3.99, M.9.343, POxy.1648.60

δολιόμυθος.definition: crafty of speech, prob. for S.Tr.839

δολιόφρων.definition: gen. crafty of mind, wily, A.Ch.947 ; E.IA1300

δολιχήρετμος.definition: long-oared, of a ship, Od.4.499, etc.; of the Phaeacians, using long oars, 8.191; Pi.O.8.20

δολιχογραφία.definition: prolix writing, AP6.327; long-continued writing, ib.65

δολιχοδρόμος.definition: running the Pl.Prt.335e, X.Smp.2.17:—Aeol. and Dor. IG12.388 , CIG 2758 , IG5.19

δολιχόουρος.definition: or long-tailed: metaph. of verses with a syll. redundant , Sch.Heph.p.290C., Eust.12.33

δολιχόσκιος.definition: casting a long shadow, Homeric epith. of Il.3.346, etc.: in later Ep. as a general epith., long, Opp.C.1.411; Nonn.D.12.181; far-reaching, Id.2.612, etc

δολοπλοκία.definition: subtlety, craft, in pl., Thgn.226, Hp.Ep.17

δολοφονέω.definition: slay by treachery, Str.5.3.2, al., Ph.1.412:—Pass., Plb.32.5.11; but freq. simply, murder , Ph.1.205, al., App.Syr.69:—Pass., D.19.194, Arist.Mir.836a16, POxy.12rv8, BGU388i 23 , etc

δολοφονία.definition: slaying by treachery, Arist.EN1131a7; murder, Plb.6.13.4

δολόφρων.definition: gen. = f. l. in A.Supp.750 ; AP7.145

δολόω.definition: beguile, ensnare, take by craft, A.Ag.273, 1636; disguise, ib.129; adulterate incense, wine, etc., Dsc.1.81, Luc.Herm.59; alloy, Gal.14.48 ; dye, Poll.7.169

δομάω.definition: = Aristid.1.821 J., cf. J.BJ5.4.2, al., Arr.An.7.22.2

δοξασμός.definition: formation of opinions; glorification, Sm.Is.13.3, Al.2 Ki.22.25

δοξοκοπία.definition: thirst for fame or popularity, Phld.Lib.p.57O., Heraclit.Ep.2, Plu.Per.5, M.Ant.11.18, Luc.Peregr.2, App.BC2.44, Hann.9, etc.; Epicur.Fr.120

δοξοκόπος.definition: = thirsting for notoriety, Telesp.39H., Ph.2.269, Muson.Fr.7p.29H., D.Chr.32.24

δοξομανής.definition: mad after fame, Chrysipp.Stoic.3.167, Ph.1.564, Iamb.VP12.58

δοξοσοφία.definition: conceit of wisdom, Pl.Sph.231b, Phlb.49a, 49d, Plu.2.999f

δοράτιον.definition: Dim. of Hdt.1.34, Th.4.34, Aen.Tact.29.6, Onos.26.1

δορατισμός.definition: fighting with spears, Plu.Pyrrh.7, Tim.28, cj. in Lib.Descr.1.6

δορατομαχέω.definition: to fight with spears, AB357, Suid. s.v

δοριάλωτος.definition: captive of the spear, taken in war, Hdt.8.74, 9.4; of persons, captive, E.Tr.518 , Isoc.4.177; Decr. ap. D.18.181, cf. Plb.23.10.6; Ion. of Tecmessa, S.Aj.211 : is a freq. v.l., as in Hp.Ep.27, X.Cyr.7.5.35, HG5.2.5, …

δοριθήρατος.definition: hunted and taken by the spear, E.Hec.103 , Tr.574

δορίκτητος.definition: won by the spear, E.Andr.155, cf. Lyc.933, etc.: in Hom., also the Ion. fem. Il.9.343, cf. A.R.1.806: Tryph.553; fem. Id.630, Plu.2.232a

δορίληπτος.definition: won by the spear, S.Aj.146 , E.Hec.478 , etc.; Ion. S.Aj.894; = Hsch

δορίμαχος.definition: fighting with the spear, Tim.Fr.14; Ion. Orac. ap. Sch.Il.2.543

δορίπονος.definition: toiling with the spear, bearing the brunt of war, A.Th.169 ; E.El.479 ; A.Th.628 ; E.IA771

δορισθενής.definition: mighty with the spear, A.Ch.158 ; AP9.475

δορκάδειος.definition: of an antelope or gazelle, Thphr.Char.5.9, Plb.26.1.8:—also written IG2.766.23, cf. PSI4.331.2, 444.2

δορυδρέπανον.definition: a kind of halbert, Pl.La.183d; esp. a large kind used for cutting off halyards in sea- fights, Str.4.4.1; in sieges, for pulling down battlements, Plb.21.27.4

δορύξενος.definition: spear-friend, i. e. war-friend, ally , A.Ag.880; Id.Ch.562, cf. S.El.46, etc.: as Adj., A.Ch.914; S.OC632

δορυξόος.definition: contr. spear- polishing: maker of spears, Plu.Pel.12:—also Ar.Pax447,1213; PTeb.278.4

δορυσσόητος.definition: = sq., of the toils of battle, S.Aj.1188

δορυσσόος.definition: contr. : :— brandishing the lance, of persons, Hes.Sc.54, A.Supp.182,985; Thgn.987: contr. S.OC1313, A.Th.125, prob. in E.Heracl.774

δορυφόρημα.definition: body-guard: used of the or mute characters on the stage, Luc.Hist.Conscr.4, Jul.Caes.310c: hence of Aridaeus, who was put up as the successor of Alexander, Plu.2.791e, cf. Id.Alex.77

δοσείω.definition: Desiderat., to be inclined to give, Hsch

δοτήρ.definition: giver, dispenser, . . Il.19.44; Hes.Sc.131; esp. of the gods, h.Hom.8.9; Pi.Pae.7.1; A.Pr.612.—Poet. form used by X.Cyr.8.1.9, and in later Prose, D.H.2.62, cf. J.AJ1.18.6, Iamb.Myst.3.31

δουλαγωγέω.definition: make a slave, treat as such, dub. in; metaph. of pleasure, etc., Longin.44.6, cf. Charito2.7; bring it into subjection, 1 Ep.Cor.9.27

δουλάριον.definition: Dim. of Ar.Th.537, Metag.19, etc.; not used of male slaves, acc. to Luc.Lex.25, but cf. Arr.Epict.2.21.11

δουλεία.definition: Ion. Anacr.114, Hdt.6.12: also; collectively, slaves, E.Ba.803; . . if the slave-class rise in rebellion, Th.5.23; Pl.Lg.776d; . . Arist.Pol.1264a36

δούλειος.definition: also Pi.Fr.223, E.Tr.1330 :—slavish, servile, Od.24.252; Thgn.535; Pi. l. c.; E.Hec.56, Andr.99, cf. Tr.1330; Pl.Lg.770e; ib.790a

δουλέκδουλος.definition: a born slave, Seleuc. ap. Ath.6.267c, D.S.10 Fr. 1

δούλευμα.definition: a service, E.Or.221; a slave, S.Ant.756, cf. E.Ion748

δουλεύω.definition: to be a slave, Hdt.2.56, And.1.138; serve, be subject, A.Pr.927, etc.; ib.463; Pl.Lg.698b; Id.Phdr.238e, etc.; X.Mem.1.6.8; Polystr.p.29 W.; make oneself a slave to one's land, i. e. give up rights that one may keep i…

δουλίς.definition: = Hyp.Fr.235, AP5.17 , IG14.1839.8: condemned by Poll.3.74

δουλογνώμων.definition: gen. of slavish mind, AB393, Suid. s.v

δουλοδιδάσκαλος.definition: teacher of slaves, title of play by Pherecr., cf. Ath.6.262b; of Theodora, Procop.Arc.15

δουλοκρατέομαι.definition: Pass., to be ruled by slaves, D.C.60.2; or, like slaves, Lib.Decl.43.35

δουλοπρεπής.definition: befitting a slave, servile, Hdt.1.126; opp. X.Mem.2.8.4 , cf. Pl.Grg.485b,518a, etc.: Sup., Phld.Herc.1457.3. Adv. D.C.61.15, cf. Gal.17.146: Sup. Cratin.403

δουλοσύνη.definition: poet. and Ion. for slavery, Od.22.423, Pi.P.12.15, A.Th.112, E.Ph.192 , Hdt.1.129, al

δουλοφανής.definition: slave-like, slavish to look on, J.BJ2.7.2

δουλόω.definition: enslave, Hdt.1.27; A.Th.254, cf. S.Tr.467; Th.2.61:—mostly in Pass., to be enslaved, Hdt.1.94,174, cf. Th.1.98; Hp.Aër.23; Th.4.34, 7.71; Men.699, cf Sam.280:—Med. , make subject to oneself, enslave, Id.1.18, 5.29, 7.…

δούλωσις.definition: enslavement, Th.3.10, Plu.Publ.21; constraint, opp. Pl.Lg.791d

δουρικλειτός.definition: famed for the spear, Homeric epith. of heroes, Il.5.55, Od.15.52

δουρικλυτός.definition: = foreg., Il.2.645, Od.15.544, Archil.3: dat. pl. A.Pers.85

δουριτυπής.definition: wood-splitting, AP6.103; smitten with the spear, IPE2.298.8

δοχή.definition: reception, entertainment, Macho ap.Ath.8.348f, LXXGe.21.8, al., PTeb.112.89 , Ev.Luc.5.29, etc.; = Hsch

δραγμός.definition: grasping, E.Cyc.170, dub. l. in Q.S.1.350

δρακόντιον.definition: a kind of fish , Hp.Int.21; edder-wort, Dracunculus vulgaris, ib.1, Thphr.HP7.12.2, Dsc.2.166

δρακοντοειδής.definition: snake-like, Peripl.M.Rubr.55. Adv. to have a serpentine course, Str.9.3.16

δρακοντοκέφαλος.definition: with a serpent's head, BGU1065.9 , Suid. s.v

δρακοντόπους.definition: gen. snake-footed, with serpents for feet, Tz.ad Lyc.63, EM371.46

δραματοποιός.definition: dramatic poet, Heph.8.1, Ps.-Luc.Philopatr.13: metaph., melodramatic, Phld.Herc.1457.12

δραματουργία.definition: = Luc.Salt.68: metaph. of life, Sopat. ap.Stob.4.5.52, Max.Tyr.7.10; the action of a play, Str.1.2.27

δραπετεύω.definition: run away, X.Mem.2.1.16; from one, Pl.Smp.216b; Luc.Somn.12; will skulk behind . . , X.HG2.4.16; Id.Ages.1.23: metaph., shirk public service, D.42.25; Pl.Men.98a; Luc.Peregr.21; Plu.2.46e; slip away, of fluids, Paul.Ae…

δραπέτης.definition: Adj., E.Or.1498 , cf. Aeschin.3.152; fugitive life, AP10.87 ; . . no skulker's lot, i. e. not a lump of earth which would fall in pieces, of the lot of Cresphontes, S.Aj.1285

δρασείω.definition: Desiderat. of have a mind to do, S.Aj.326,585, E.Ph.1208, Med.93, Ar.Pax62

δραστέος.definition: to be done, S.Tr.1204; one must do, Id.OT1443, E.IA1024, D.Chr.12.16

δρέπω.definition: Ep. impf. h.Cer.425: aor. 1; Med., pluck for oneself, cull, . . Od.12.357; . . h.Cer.429; Pi.N.2.9; Pl.Ion534b; Theoc.18.40; AP12.125 ; Jul.Or.7.207c; Orph.Fr.228; cull the fruits of murder, A.Th.718, cf. Bion1.22: ab…

δριμυφαγέω.definition: live on acrid food, Sor.1.64, Paul.Aeg.4.1

δριμυφαγία.definition: acrid diet, Dsc.2.31 , Philum. ap. Orib.45.29.13, Aët.16.75

δρομαγετέω.definition: act as clerk of the course, IG12.134, 258

δρομαδάριος.definition: or = Lat. dromedarius, POxy.1652a6, BGU 827v, etc

δρομαῖος.definition: also E.Alc.245 :—running; epith. of Apollo, as patron of racing, Plu.2.724c, IG5.497, al

δρομάς.definition: running, E.Supp.1000 ; the whirling wheel, S.Ph.678 ; Ar.Fr.420; dromedary, D.S.19.37, Str.15.2.10, J.AJ6.14.6, Plu.Alex.31: also with a neut., E.Hel.1301 ; Id.Or.837 . 2. wildly roaming, frantic, Id.Hipp.549 , Tr.42;…

δρύϊνος.definition: oaken, Od.21.43, Hp.Fract.13, E.Ba.1103, etc.; a fire of oak-wood, Theoc.9.19; honey from the hollow of an oak, AP9.72 ); Mon.Anc. Gr.17.24

δρύκαρπον.definition: acorn or similar fruit, Lyc.83, Eust.773.49

δρυοβάλανος.definition: acorn, Str.15.3.18: sg. in collect. sense, Id.3.3.7

δρυοκολάπτης.definition: woodpecker, of which Arist. distinguishes four species, the great black, Picus martius, the green, Picus viridis, and the spotted . Picus major and minor, HA593a5, cf. 614b7, Str.5.4.2; = Lat. picus, D.H.1.14:—also Ar…

δρυοτόμος.definition: = Aesop.35, Gal.13.573, etc. v.l. in Q.S.1.250.]

δρυψογέρων.definition: worn-out old man, and coquette, Hsch.; also, = Id

δρωπακίζω.definition: apply a depilatory, Orib.Eup.4.7:—Med., Arr.Epict.3.22.10, Hierocl.Facet.64:—Pass., Luc.Demon.50

δυηπάθια.definition: poet. misery, A.R.4.1395, APl.4.113 , Hsch.:—written EM291.10

δυναμοδύναμις.definition: square multiplied by square, fourth power, HeroMetr.1.17; fourth power of unknown quantity , Dioph.Def.1 , al.: —hence the fraction 1/x4, Id.Def.3, al

δυναμόκυβος.definition: square multiplied by cube, fifth power, Hippol.Haer.1.2.10; fifth power of unknown quantity , Dioph.Def.1 , al.:—hence the fraction 1/x5, Id.Def.3, al

δυναμόω.definition: strengthen, LXXEc.10.10, Thd.Da.9.27; in magic, put power into, PMag.Leid.W.7.16; ib.V.8.19; PMag.Par.1.197:—Pass., PMag.Berol.2.121

δυναστεία.definition: power, lordship, domination, S.OT593; close oligarchy, opp. Th.4.78, cf. And.2.27, X.HG5.4.46, etc.; Pl.Plt.291d; opp. Arist.Pol.1272b10; distd.fr. ib.1292b10, cf. 1293a31: in pl., of the Roman Senate, D.C.52.1

δυνάστευμα.definition: in pl., natural resources, LXX3 Ki.2.46c

δυνάστης.definition: lord, master, ruler, of Zeus, S.Ant.608 ; the chief men in a state, Hdt.2.32, cf. Pl.R.473d, etc.; petty chief, princelet, Th.7.33, etc.; Plb.9.23.5, cf. 10.34.2, Posidon.50 J., Str.17.3.25; of the stars, A.Ag.6

δυνατοτερέω.definition: to be more capable of financial burdens, PFlor.296.37

δυοκαιδεκάδελτος.definition: or the Laws of the Twelve Tables, Lyd.Mag.1.26,42

δυσάδελφος.definition: unhappy in one's brothers, A.Th.871 , Vett.Val.18.5

δυσαισθησία.definition: low degree of sensibility, Ti. Locr.102e, Gal.7.55 , prob. in Phld.Piet.67

δυσαίσθητος.definition: Pass., scarcely perceptible, Alex.Aphr.in Sens.85.24; hard to trace, Poll.5.12

δυσαιτιολόγητος.definition: hard to account for, Ph.2.644, Gal.13.605

δυσαλθής.definition: = sq., Hp.Art.41, Cass.Pr.1; deadly, Nic.Al.12, 157, Luc.Dem.Enc.13: neut. pl. as Adv., Q.S.12.408

δυσαλλοίωτος.definition: hard to alter, Gal.Protr.11; hard to digest, Hp.Alim.49; Alex.Aphr.Pr.1.83

δυσάλυκτος.definition: hard to escape, Nic.Al.251, 537, LXXWi.17.17, Man.3.247

δυσάλωτος.definition: hard to catch or take; hard to conquer, A.Pr.167 ; Luc.Abd.18 ; immune, Gal.4.742; Sor.1.32 : c. gen., beyond reach of ills, S.OC1723

δυσαναβλαστέω.definition: prob. f.l. for well up with difficulty, Plu.2.688e

δυσανάγνωστος.definition: hard to read, prob. for Plb.3.32.1

δυσανάγωγος.definition: hard to throw up, Dsc.1.1, cf. Androm. ap. Gal.13.28

δυσανάδοτος.definition: hard to assimilate, Diph.Siph. ap. Ath.3.91e, Gal.19.364, Hippiatr.1

δυσανακάθαρτος.definition: hard to cleanse, Gal. ap. Orib.Syn.9.3.8

δυσανάκλητος.definition: hard to call back, Plu.2.74e; hard to restore, of hysterics, Sor.2.29 , cf. Herod.Med. in Rh.Mus.58.74; or to good spirits, Max.Tyr.33.6. Adv. to be hard to restore to one's senses, Dsc.Alex.16

δυσανακόμιστος.definition: hard to carry upwards, Plu.Rom.28:—poet. hard to recall, A.Eu.262

δυσανάκρατος.definition: hard to mix or temper, Plu.2.1024d

δυσανάληπτος.definition: hard to recover; hard to recover from, Jul.Or.6.181a. Adv. to be in a bad way for recovery, Ruf. ap. Orib.8.47.4

δυσανάλυτος.definition: hard to analyse, Porph.in Cat.132.9. Adv. Simp.in Cat.212.16

δυσανάπνευστος.definition: offensive to inhalation; transpiring with difficulty, Gal.7.287

δυσανάσφαλτος.definition: hardly recovering from an illness, Hp.Alim.28

δυσανασχετέω.definition: bear ill, Th.7.71; to be greatly vexed, Plu.Cam.35, Plb.16.12.5; Phalar.Ep.37; J.AJ13.16.2: abs., Eus.Mynd.59, Aët.8.44

δυσανάσχετος.definition: hard to bear, intolerable; Act., bearing hardly, in Adv. A.D.Synt.218.9, cf. Poll.3.130

δυσανάτρεπτος.definition: hard to overthrow, Plu.Caes.4, cf. Gal.18.604

δυσάνεκτος.definition: = I, interpol. in X.Mem.2.2.8, cf. Gal.7.181. Adv. Poll.3.130

δυσάνιος.definition: soon vexed, ill to please, Antipho Soph.89, CritiasFr.42 D., Men.803 ); opp. Arist.Phgn.805b6; vexed, annoyed, in Comp. Phld.Acad.Ind.p.50 M

δυσανταγώνιστος.definition: hard to struggle against, Paus.1.17.6, D.L.2.134, Jul.Or.1.34b

δυσάντης.definition: = sq. II, ib.6.310, cf. Musae.324; hard to climb, Ph.1.255; Opp.C.4.432

δυσάντητος.definition: disagreeable to meet, boding of ill; hard to withstand, Plu.2.118c; Procl.H.3.5; Max.Tyr.5.3

δυσαντίβλεπτος.definition: hard to look in the face, Plu.Marc.23; Corn.ND20; hard to face, Syrian.in Metaph.178.30; hard to vie with, Philostr. Jun.Im.Praef.; Agathin. ap. Orib.10.7.6

δυσαντίλεκτος.definition: hard to gainsay, D.H.5.18: metaph., J.AJ18.9.5

δυσαντίρρητος.definition: = foreg., gloss on Hsch., EM406.7. Adv. Plb.9.31.7

δυσαπαλλακτία.definition: the quality of being difficult to get rid of, persistency, Pl.Phlb.46c

δυσαπάλλακτος.definition: hard to get rid of, Hp.Nat.Mul.40; S.Tr.959 ; Isoc.10.28; Arist.PA671b9, cf. Cat.10a4: c. gen., having difficulty in bringing forth, Id.HA587b1; a person hard to draw away from . . , Pl.Tht.195c. Adv. Eust.1389.46, cf…

δυσαπόβλητος.definition: hard to get rid of, Alex.Aphr.Febr.19; hard to cast away, Olymp.in Alc.p.51 C.; hard to lose, Id.in Cat.116.25, cf. Ammon.in Cat.82.8, Simp.in Cat.228.23

δυσαποδίωκτος.definition: hard to drive away, Sch. Theoc.10.11

δυσαπόδοτος.definition: hard to render or define, S.E.M.7.242, Bacch.Harm.95

δυσαποκατάστασις.definition: difficulty of recovering, mortal sickness, Erot. s.v

δυσαποκατάστατος.definition: hard to restore, M.Ant.11.8; hard to recover from, Phld.Ir.p.63 W

δυσαπόκριτος.definition: hard to answer, Luc.Vit.Auct.22; Act., hardly answering, Paul. Aeg.3.9

δυσαπολόγητος.definition: hard to defend or excuse, Plb.1.10.4, cf. Ph.1.562, J.AJ16.4.2; hard to answer, Aristeas213; hard to explain, Str.4.1.7. Adv. Eust.147.23

δυσαπόνιπτος.definition: hard to wash off or out, Zen.1.47, Sch.E.Ph.63: Comp., Theol.Ar.22

δυσαπόπτωτος.definition: not apt to fall off, Thphr.CP1.11.8

δυσαπόσπαστος.definition: hard to tear away, Posidon.15 J; from which it is hard to tear oneself away, Ph.2.11, 14; Charito5.8

δυσαπότρεπτος.definition: hard to dissuade, refractory, X.Mem.4.1.4, Aristaenet.1.28

δυσαπότριπτος.definition: hard to rub off and so get rid of, Macar.8.47, cf. Ph.1.459, 615 , Thessal. ap. Gal.10.252; of persons, Plu.2.55e

δυσαρεστέω.definition: suffer annoyance, Arist.HA560b24; to be; c. dat. pers., to be displeasing to, Id.7.5.6, D.S.18.62; Ph.2.6:—also Med. Plu.2.94d, cf. Iamb.VP35.255

δυσαρέστημα.definition: Medic., malaise, distress, Antyll. ap. Stob.4.37.15, Sor.1.26

δυσαρεστία.definition: distress, malaise, Herod.Med. in Hermes40.584, prob. in Aët.16.18 , Hierocl.in CA11p.442M

δυσάρεστος.definition: hard to appease, implacable, A.Eu.928; ill-pleased, at a thing, Luc.Nav.46; ill to please, fastidious, peevish, E.Or.232, cf. Isoc.1.31, 12.8, X.Mem.3.13.3 , Diph.63, Nicostr.31 , Plu.2.128d; Polystr.Herc.1520.1; disp…

δυσαριστοτόκεια.definition: unhappy mother of the noblest son, as Thetis calls herself, Il.18.54

δύσαρκτος.definition: hard to govern, A.Ch.1024; J.AJ4.2.1; Plu.Luc.2; App.BC2.149

δυσαυλία.definition: ill or hard lodging, A.Ag.555 , Ph.1.195

δυσαυξής.definition: hardly or slowly growing, Arist.Aud.802a25, Thphr.CP1.8.4, J.AJ3.1.3:— also Thphr.CP1.8.2

δυσαφαίρετος.definition: hard to take away, Arist.EN1095b26; hard to remove, of an application, Gal.12.356

δυσβάστακτος.definition: intolerable, grievous to be borne, LXXPr.27.3, Ev.Matt.23.4, Plu.2.915f, etc.; of persons, Antisth. ap. Ph.2.449

δυσβατοποιέομαι.definition: make impassable, dub. l. in X.Eq.Mag.8.9

δυσβοήθητος.definition: hard to help or cure, Hp.Coac.491, D.S.3.47, 11.15, Paul. Aeg.5.29: Comp., Dsc.Eup.2.159. Adv. Gal.5.122

δύσβολος.definition: throwing badly, esp. with dice, Poll.9.94

δυσβουλία.definition: ill counsel, A.Th.802, Ag.1609, S.Ant.95: pl., ib.1269

δυσβράκανος.definition: hard to deal with, Cratin.404; cf

δύσγαμος.definition: ill-wedded, E.Ph.1047 ; Lyc.1089, cf. Paul.Al.N.2; of Menelaus, E.Tr.1114; Luc.Trag.49

δυσγενής.definition: low-born, E.Ion1477, Ar.Ra.1219, etc; low-minded, mean, E.El.363, etc.; Com. ap. Stob.4.30.6a

δυσγεφύρωτος.definition: hard to make a bridge over, Str.4.3.3

δυσγεώργητος.definition: hard to till or cultivate, Id.17.3.25

δυσγνώριστος.definition: hard to recognize, Gal.7.804, al., Poll.5.150. Adv. ib.160

δύσγνωστος.definition: hard to understand, Pl.Alc.2.147c; hard to recognize, Plb.3.78.4: Sup., Aen. Tact.25.2

δυσγοήτευτος.definition: hard to seduce by enchantments, Pl.R.413e

δυσγράμματος.definition: hard to write, Aristid.2.360 J; unlearned, Philostr.VS2.1.10

δυσδαίμων.definition: gen. ill-starred, unhappy, Emp.9.4, A.Th.827, S.Ant.274; Id.OT1302 ; Pl.Lg.905c; Ti.Locr.104d; of a person, BGU1024 vii 24 : Comp. And.2.9. Adv. Eust.1064.44

δυσδάκρυτος.definition: sorely wept, A.Ag.442; Act., sorely weeping, AP12.80 ; tears of anguish, ib.7.476

δυσδάμαστος.definition: hard to subdue: hence, hard to work, Sch.Hes.Sc.122

δυσδιάβατος.definition: hard to get through, Aen.Tact.8.1, cf. X.An.6.5.19; Plb.1.39.13; D.S.17.93

δυσδιάγνωστος.definition: hard to distinguish, Cic.Att.5.4.1, D.H.2.71, Gal.9.433, etc

δυσδιάλυτος.definition: hard to dissolve, Arist.Pr.870b31; hard to digest, Philotim. ap. Ath.2.53f, Gal.16.760

δυσδιάπνευστος.definition: slow to evaporate, Thphr.CP1.2.4; slow to perspire, Herod.Med. ap. Orib.5.27.3

δυσδιάσπαστος.definition: hard to break, Plb.15.15.7; hard to pull up, of a palisade, Ph.Bel.82.35

δυσδιαστατέω.definition: to be unstable, dub. in Plu.2.993e

δυσδιάστατος.definition: hard to separate, Herod.Med. in Rh.Mus.58.90

δυσδιάφευκτος.definition: or hard to escape, Suid., Hsch

δυσδιαφόρητος.definition: hard to disperse or dissipate; hardly evaporating, Id.10.657; not excreting readily, Id.17.188; Alex.Trall.8.2; cf

δυσδιαχώρητος.definition: indigestible, Arist.Pr.927b21; Act., costive, Alex.Aphr.Pr.1.90, Sever.p.6 D

δυσδιέγερτος.definition: hard to be roused from, Gal.19.413, cf. Herod. Med. in Rh.Mus.58.77

δυσδιεξίτητος.definition: hard to get through, v.l. in D.S.3.44

δυσδιερεύνητος.definition: hard to search thoroughly, Pl.R.432c, D.C.51.26, Them.Or.21.254d

δυσδιόδευτος.definition: = Hsch.; of a child's tissues, Sor.1.95

δυσδιοίκητος.definition: hard to manage, J.BJ2.16.4; hard to digest, Xenocr.31, Sor.1.93

δυσδιόριστος.definition: hard to delimit, S.E.M.5.74; hard to distinguish, ib.7.416

δυσεγχείρητος.definition: hard to take in hand, J.AJ15.11.2

δυσέγχωστος.definition: hard to dam up, prob. in Str.16.1.10

δυσείκαστος.definition: hard to make out, of Thucydides' style, D.H.Lys.4, cf. Luc.Icar.4

δυσείσβολος.definition: hard to enter or invade, of Laconia, E.Fr.1083, cf. Aen.Tact.16.17; of a river, Str.4.1.8: Sup. least accessible, of Locris, Th.3.101

δυσέκβατος.definition: hard to get out of, D.C.56.19, Nonn.D.45.269

δυσεκβίαστος.definition: hard to overpower, Plu.2.127a, cf.Cor.2, Eun.VSp.500 B

δυσέκδυτος.definition: hard to shake off, Hsch. s.v

δυσεκθέρμαντος.definition: hard to warm, Plu.2.625a, Gal.6.608, Antyll. ap.Orib.10.13.9. Adv. Id.ib.10.29.3, Gal.10.674

δυσεκκόμιστος.definition: hard to carry out, Hsch. and Suid. s.v

δυσέκλυτος.definition: hard to undo, A.Fr.375 ; Ph.1.192, cf. Vett.Val.71.23, al. Adv. indissolubly, A.Pr.60

δυσεκμόχλευτος.definition: hard to dislodge, of disease, Antyll. ap. Orib.10.29.3

δυσέκνευστος.definition: hard to swim out of, Max.Tyr.17.10

δυσέκνιπτος.definition: hard to wash out, Pl.R.378d; hard to cleanse, Ael.NA1.48

δυσεκπέρατος.definition: hard to pass out from, hard to escape, E.Hipp.678 , 883

δυσέκπλυτος.definition: hard to wash out, Ph.2.182,487; hard to cleanse, Ael.NA1.48: metaph., Ph.1.558

δυσεκπόρευτος.definition: hard to get out of, Ph.Bel.79.25; J.AJ13.2.4

δυσεκπύητος.definition: hard to bring to suppuration, Gal.11.119, Paul.Aeg.4.18

δυσέκτηκτος.definition: hard to melt, dub. in Hp.Alim.51

δυσέκφευκτος.definition: hard to escape from, Tim.Pers.130, Theodect.10, Plb.1.77.7, Man.4.477; hardly escaping, Tim.Pers.140. Adv. APl.4.198

δυσέκφορος.definition: hard to pronounce or utter, Phld.Po.994 Fr.22, 1676.8, D.H.Comp.12, 16 ; Cat.Cod.Astr.2.167. Adv. Str.14.2.28

δυσελπιστέω.definition: to have scarce a hope, Plb.2.10.8, 4.60.4:—Pass., to be despaired of, Epicur.Sent.Vat.17

δυσελπιστία.definition: despondency, Arist.VV1251b25, Plb.1.39.14, Telesp.35 H., Ph.1.119, App.BC4.12

δυσέλπιστος.definition: = Lyr.Adesp.138; unhoped for, unexpectedly, X.Cyr.6.1.47, cf. Vett. Val. 124.25

δυσέμβατος.definition: hard to walk on, rugged, Th.4.10; inaccessible, D.P.1150

δυσέμβλητος.definition: hard to set, of dislocations, Hp.Art.71

δυσέμβολος.definition: = foreg., Id.Fract.38; hard to enter, X.HG6.5.24; Arist.Pol.1326b41; Plb.3.49.7, cf. J.AJ17.2.1

δυσενέργητος.definition: sluggish, Sch. Ar.Pl.313; of food, badly digested, Sor.1.34

δυσεντερία.definition: dysentery, Hp.Aph.3.12 , al., Hdt.8.115, Pl.Ti.86a , Arist.Pr.861b16, etc

δυσέντευκτος.definition: unpleasant to meet, physically repulsive, Thphr.Char.19; but more usu. unpleasant to deal with, Plb.5.34.4, Plu.2.27e; Ph.2.520, J.AJ13.2.1

δυσεξάγωγος.definition: difficult to carry off or get rid of, Hp.Insomn.89, Arist.Pr.871a19

δυσεξάλειπτος.definition: hard to wipe out, Plb.39.3.1; D.S.3.6; Longin.7.3; Corn.Rh.p.353 H

δυσεξέλεγκτος.definition: hard to refute, Pl.Phd.85c; hard to discover, D.H.3.5

δυσεξέλευστος.definition: hard to get out of, Tz.H.11.556

δυσεξέλικτος.definition: hard to unfold, involved, D.H.Th.29, cf. Amm.2.2, Plu.Brut.13; Luc.Trag.25; twisted, contorted, Ael.NA14.8

δυσεξεύρετος.definition: hard to find out, Id.HA611a26, Plu.2.407f

δυσεξήγητος.definition: hard to explain, Darius ap.D.L.9.13, Gal.17 .71

δυσεξίλλητος.definition: hard to unravel, Cic. Att.5.10.3 . Adv., in form v.l. in Sch.Theoc.14.51

δυσεξίτηλος.definition: not easily perishing, Str.11.8.7, cf. Plu.2.696d, Philum.Ven.4.3

δυσεπανόρθωτος.definition: hard to correct or reform, Vett. Val.77.6; TheoProg.12

δυσεπέκτατος.definition: hard to extend or distend, Gal.8.288,al

δυσεπίβολος.definition: hard to assail, Aen.Tact.8.1 codd.; risky to undertake, Peripl. M.Rubr.39; unsuccessful, Paul.Al.N.4

δυσεπιβούλευτος.definition: hard to attack secretly; hard to damage, Apollod.Poliorc.139.7

δυσεπίγνωστος.definition: hard to identify or find out, SIG1023.9 , App.BC1.18

δυσεπίμικτος.definition: disinclined for intercourse, Str.11.2.2: abs., unsociable, Id.3.3.8; Plu.2.917c, Porph.Abst.4.6

δυσεπινόητος.definition: hard to understand, M.Ant.6.17; hard to devise or plan out, Jul.Or.1.12b

δυσεπίστροφος.definition: hard to turn or guide, App.Mith.42

δυσεπίσχετος.definition: hard to check, of bleeding, Gal.19.457, Aret.CA2.6. Adv. Gal.7.725, Herod.Med. in Rh.Mus.58.99

δυσεπίτευκτος.definition: hard to accomplish; hard to treat, Hippiatr.26

δυσεπιχείρητος.definition: hard to attack, Id.Top.159a3; ib.158b16: Sup. ib.158b8; of a person, J.BJ4.3.10, Plu.2.281a, App.Pun.118

δυσέργεια.definition: difficulty, Sor.2.53, Orib.45.18.14; functional defect, Paul.Aeg.6.42, al

δυσεργής.definition: difficult, App.Hisp.73, al.; OGI502.6 : Comp., of an operation, Antyll. ap.Orib.44.23.23; making it hard to work, Plu.2.1129d

δυσεργία.definition: difficulty in working or construction, Ph.Bel.56.42, cf. HeroAut.23.8 , Plu.Aem.16; difficulty in pronouncing, Phld.Po.2.42; inability to exert oneself, Hp.VM10 ; inability to act, App.Syr.19

δύσεργος.definition: hard to work, Thphr.HP5.1.1; hard to effect, difficult, Plb.28.8.3, Ph.1.272 ; App.Hisp.63 ; J.BJ5.12.1. Adv. Plu.Demetr.43

δυσέριστος.definition: pertaining to unholy strife, S.El.1385 ; Cleanth.Stoic.1.122

δυσερμήνευτος.definition: hard to interpret, Ep.Hebr.5.11, Gal.11.454, Cat.Cod.Astr.1.114.26; hard to describe, D.S.2.52; Ph.1.649

δύσερμος.definition: not favoured by Hermes, unlucky, Suid.:—hence ill luck, Hsch., EM291.49

δυσερωτιάω.definition: to be desperately in love, Ach.Tat.5.1, Plu.Fr.21.2

δυσευνήτωρ.definition: Dor. ill bedfellow, A.Th.293 :—expld. by ill-bedded, in Sch.ad loc

δυσεύρετος.definition: hard to find out, A.Pr.816; hard to find or get, X.Mem.3.14.7, Secund.Sent.11; Plu.2.97b

δυσέφικτος.definition: hard to come at, Plb.31.25.3, Plu.2.65e, Phld.Rh.2.119 S.; Ecphant. ap. Stob.4.7.64; hard to understand, Vett.Val.272.8, al

δυσέφοδος.definition: hard to get at, inaccessible, D.S.1.57 ; Phld.Rh.1.325 S

δυσέψανος.definition: hard to digest, Suid. s. vv

δυσέψητος.definition: = foreg., Phryn.PSp.33 B.; hard to cook, Gal.6.541

δυσζήτητος.definition: hard to seek or track, X.Cyn.8.1, Poll.5.50

δυσήκεστος.definition: hard to heal or cure, Hp.Fract.29, AP3.19

δυσηκοΐα.definition: hardness of hearing, Dsc.5.17, Plu.2.1073d, Vett.Val.109.31; disobedience, Plu.2.794d

δυσήκοος.definition: hard of hearing, Ph.2.35; ill-sounding, terrible to hear, prob. in S.Fr.220; unpleasant to the ear, Demetr.Eloc.48, Poll.2.117, Philostr.VS1.12; of an orator, Eun.VSp.456 B

δυσήλατος.definition: hard to drive through or over, Poll.1.186

δυσηλεγής.definition: Homeric epith. of death and war, bringing bitter grief, cruel, ruthless, Od.22.325, Il.20.154; . . cruel frosts, Hes.Op.506; Id.Th.652; also of men, Thgn.795; Max.87

δυσημερέω.definition: have an unlucky day, be unlucky, Pherecr.98; D.H.1.57

δυσημερία.definition: Dor. unlucky day: mishap, misery, A.Fr.236; S.Fr.591, cf. Plu.Eum.9

δυσήμερος.definition: hard to tame, restive, Str.3.3.8, Ptol.Tetr.56

δυσηνιόχητος.definition: hard to hold in, ungovernable, Luc.Abd.17

δυσήνυτος.definition: hard to accomplish, J.BJ5.12.1; also Hsch

δύσηρις.definition: = I, Pi.O.6.19, Axiop.1.4: Att. form of acc. to Moer.126

δυσηχής.definition: Dor. ill-sounding, Phld.Po.2.16, v.l. in D.H.Comp.14; giving a dull sound, of metals, Plu.2.721c; Emp.100.19:— in Hom., epith. of Il.2.686 , al.; and of Il.16.442, al. , cf. Apollon.Lex.), of Emp.136.1; of ill-repute,…

δυσθανατέω.definition: to be loath to die, Hdt.9.72; struggle against death, die hard, Pl.R.406b, Thphr.HP3.11.3, Plu.Ant.77, etc.; also, to be sick to death with desire, Ph.2.167; to be deadly obstinate, ib.100: abs., to be in deadly terro…

δυσθάνατος.definition: bringing a hard death, Hp.Prorrh.1.55; E.Ion1051

δυσθέατος.definition: ill to look on, A.Pr.69; hard to see, Plu.2.966b, cf. Ael.NA9.61

δυσθεράπευτος.definition: hard to cure, Hp.Medic.10, S.Aj.609 ; Ph.1.334

δυσθετέω.definition: to be dissatisfied; mostly in Med., abs., to be vexed, X.Cyr.2.2.5; Plb.33.17.1; to be in straits, Id.8.5.4

δυσθεώρητος.definition: hard to observe, Arist.HA511b13; hard to understand or reduce to theory, Ph.Bel.49.19, cf. Plb.3.31.7, Phld.Rh.1.141 S., Ph.2.84

δυσθήρατος.definition: hard to catch, Arist.HA615a22, Plu.Pomp.38: metaph., Ph.1.234; Plu.Per.13, cf. Ph.2.217, al

δυσθησαύριστος.definition: hard to store, Pl.Criti.115b, cf. Arist.Mu.401a5

δύσθλαστος.definition: hard to crush, tough, Thphr.HP8.4.1 , Gal.UP11.17

δυσθρήνητος.definition: loud-wailing, most mournful, S.Ant.1211; E.IT144 :—also gloss on Apollon.Lex

δυσθυμαίνω.definition: to be dispirited, despond, h. Cer.362

δυσθυμέω.definition: = foreg., Hdt.8.100, Onos.10.26; Plu.Tim.34:—Med., to be melancholy, angry, Democr.286, E.Med.91

δύσθυμος.definition: desponding, melancholy, S.El.218 , X.Cyr.5.2.34, Arist.Pr.955a17 , Phld.Herc.1251.10; S.El.550; = Plu.Per.15. Adv. Plb.1.87.1, Phld.Mort.27: Comp. Pl.Phd.85b

δυσίατος.definition: Ion. hard to heal, Hp.Art.14 , cf. Cass.Pr.1 ; an ill that none can cure, A.Ag.1103 ; E.Med.520; Pl.Lg.916a, cf. Ph.1.40, al.; of persons, implacable, Them.Or.15.192c. Adv. Gal.18.273

δυσίππαστος.definition: = sq., Anon.Hist. in Rev.Ét.Gr.5.320, Sch.Pl.Mx.240c, cf. Poll.1.186

δυσκάθαρτος.definition: hard to purify, Ph.1.239, al; hard to satisfy by purification or atonement, of the house of the Labdacidae in which murders never ceased, S.Ant.1284 ; Ar.Pax1250

δυσκάθεκτος.definition: hard to hold in, X.Mem.4.1.3 ; Plu.Num.4: metaph., Corn.ND30; Luc.Tim.29 ; hard to keep in mind, retain, Plu.2.408b

δυσκάθοδος.definition: hard to go down into, Conon35.1

δυσκαμπής.definition: hard to bend, Plu.2.650d, Aret.SD2.3: Comp., Sabin. ap. Orib.9.19.2

δυσκαρτέρητος.definition: hard to endure, Ph.2.73, Plu.Phoc.4, etc. Adv. Porph.Marc.8, Herod.Med. ap. Aët.9.2

δυσκαταγώνιστος.definition: hard to overcome, Plb.15.15.8, D.H.3.7; hard to refute, Id.Rh.8.3; impregnability, Corn.ND20

δυσκατάθετος.definition: hard to bring, f.l. for Iamb.VP31.194

δυσκάτακτος.definition: hard to break, Thphr.HP3.7.4, Dsc.3.22, Apollod.Poliorc.139.8

δυσκατάληπτος.definition: hard to comprehend, D.S.1.3, Ph.2.216, M.Ant.5.10

δυσκατάλυτος.definition: hard to bring to an end, Str.14.1.28; hard to overthrow, J.BJ4.5.5

δυσκαταμάθητος.definition: hard to learn or understand, Isoc.10.11, Pl.Plt.303d , D.H.Th.9. Adv. Isoc.2.33

δυσκατανόητος.definition: hard to understand, D.S.5.14, cf. Plu.2.47c

δυσκατάπαυστος.definition: hard to check, A.Ch.470 ; LXX3 Ma.5.7; of persons, Plu.Alex.31; restless, E.Med.109 ; Thphr.Vent.35

δυσκατάπληκτος.definition: hard to keep in awe, Plb.1.67.4

δυσκαταπόνητος.definition: hard to execute, M.Ant.6.19, Arr.Epict.3.12.8; hard to digest, Sor.2.32

δυσκαταποσία.definition: difficulty of swallowing, Herod.Med. in Rh.Mus.58.86, Philum. ap. Aët.8.48

δυσκαταποτέω.definition: have difficulty in swallowing, Herod.Med. ap. Orib.5.30.12

δυσκατάποτος.definition: hard to swallow, Arist.Sens.443b12, Archig. ap. Gal.12.976

δυσκατάστατος.definition: hard to restore or rally, X.Cyr.5.3.43

δυσκατέργαστος.definition: hard to work, Str.17.1.33; hard to tame, Agatharch.76 ; hard to overcome, Luc.Tyr.15

δυσκατόρθωτος.definition: hard to succeed in; hard to set right, remedy, J.AJ2.5.6

δυσκέλαδος.definition: ill-sounding, shrieking, Il.16.357; envy with its tongue of malice, Hes.Op.196; A.Th.867 , cf. Fr.451 I; E.Ion1098

δυσκινησία.definition: Ion. difficulty of moving, Hp.Aph.3.17, Arist.GA780a25, PA685a8

δυσκίνητος.definition: hard to move, Pl.Ti.56a, Ph.2.227; in mental relations, Pl.R.503d; Arist.VV1250a5; Id.PA686a30; Id.Cat.9a10; obstinacy, Phld.Lib.p.55 O.; of language, clumsiness, Id.Po.994.35. Adv. Pl.R.503d

δυσκλεής.definition: inglorious, Il.9.22 ; infamous, shameful, of persons and things, A.Pr.243; Id.Pers.444; E.Hel.270. cf.X.Cyr.3.3.53, LXX3 Ma.3.23 . Adv. S.El.1006, E.Hel.993 codd., Plu.2.169a

δυσκληδόνιστος.definition: of ill name, boding ill, Luc.Am.39

δυσκλήρημα.definition: piece of ill luck, Plb.30.20.9 ; D.S.32.22

δυσκοιτέω.definition: to have bad nights, Hp.VM10, Acut.30

δυσκολαίνω.definition: impf. Pl.Phlb.26d: fut; cause trouble or annoyance, Hp.Prorrh.1.109

δυσκολία.definition: discontent, peevishness, Ar.V.106; of things, difficulty, D.5.1, Arist.Pol.1281a14, etc.; ib.1263a11; J.AJ2.7.4

δυσκόλλητος.definition: hard to glue together, Gal.11.124, 133; ill-glued or fastened, loose, Luc.Hist.Conscr.11

δυσκολόκαμπτος.definition: hard to bend: an intricate flourish in singing, Ar.Nu.971

δύσκολος.definition: I. of persons, prop. hard to satisfy with food : but, generally, hard to please, discontented, fretful, peevish, Ar.V.942; E.Ba.1251; Pl.Lg.649e, cf. Arist.EN1108a30, etc.; Pl.Lg.791c; of animals, intractable, Id.Tht.…

δυσκόμιστος.definition: hard to bear, intolerable, S.Ant.1346 ; E.HF1422

δυσκρασία.definition: bad temperament, of the air, Str.6.4.1, Plu.Alex.58 ; Stoic.3.216; Ph.1.29

δυσκράτητος.definition: hard to control, D.S.3.3; ungovernable, ill-disciplined, J.AJ19.4.1; App.Syr.61

δύσκρατος.definition: of bad temperament, Str.2.3.1, cf. Gal.9.912. Adv. Id.10.518; Ps.-Plu.Vit.Hom.202

δυσκρινής.definition: hard to distinguish, Plu.2.922a; = sq., Aët.5.10

δύσκριτος.definition: hard to discern or interpret, A.Pr.458; ib.486; Id.Ag.981 , cf. S.Tr.949 ; hard to determine, doubtful, Hp.Aph.3.8; but there was an obscure crisis, Id.Epid.3.12; . . . . difficult of solution, Id.Aph.1.12, Pl.R.433c.…

δύσκτητος.definition: hard to come by, Plb.3.32.1; Phld.Herc.1251.4

δυσκυβέω.definition: to be unlucky at dice, Ath.15.666d, Poll.9.94

δυσκωφέω.definition: to be hard of hearing, Gal.12.653, AP7.731 , Dsc.4.162

δύσκωφος.definition: hard of hearing, Hp.Coac.193, Arist.Insomn.459b21, LXXEx.4.11, Str.14.2.21; Plu.2.13e

δύσληπτος.definition: hard to take hold of, Sor.1.88; hard to catch, Ph.2.366, cf. Luc.Anach.27; hard to comprehend, Str.13.4.12, A.D.Synt.225.28, Plu.2.17d

δύσλυτος.definition: insoluble, of a problem, Luc.JTr.12, Alex.Aphr.in Metaph.223.2; Plu.Fr.25.3; hard to refute, Alex.Aphr.in Top.558.25

δυσμαθής.definition: hard to learn, Id.Ag.1255; Act., slow at learning, dull, Pl.R.358a, etc.: Comp., Plu.2.992d: Sup., Ph.2.175, Jul.Or.7.225b. Adv. Pl.R.503d

δυσμάλακτος.definition: hard to soften, Ruf. ap. Orib.8.24.22

δυσμεναίνω.definition: bear ill-will, against another, E.Med.874; D.18.217; App.Pun.60: abs., Ph.1.145

δυσμένεια.definition: Ion. ill-will, enmity, S.El.619; ib.1124; E.Heracl.991: in Prose, Democr.191, Antipho4.1.3, etc.; Isoc.5.68, Pl.R.500c; Id.Prt.316d

δυσμενής.definition: hostile, Il.5.488; rarely of things, S.El.440; X.Mem.2.6.21, cf. E.Alc.617

δυσμετάβολος.definition: = foreg., Damocr. ap. Gal.13.1003. Adv. ib.1004

δυσμετάδοτος.definition: not imparting freely, Str.17.1.29: c.gen., reluctant to part with, Phld.Herc.1251.20

δυσμετάθετος.definition: hard to alter, of persons, opinionated, Plb.12.26d.5; Plu.2.799b; hard to remove, Gal.11.215

δυσμετακίνητος.definition: hard to shift, J.AJ16.11.8; Plu.2.288d, Eust.1733.32. Adv. Alex.Trall.1.16

δυσμετάκλαστος.definition: hard to break or move, Sch.S.OT12

δυσμετάκλητος.definition: hard to cure of a habit, Gp.19.2.13

δυσμετάστρεπτος.definition: hard to divert, Gal.19.489. Adv. gloss on Apollon.Lex

δυσμεταχείριστος.definition: hard to manage, Pl.Lg.808d; hard to attack, Hdt.7.236, J.BJ1.7.1; of the tortoise's shell, Hierocl.p.13 A

δυσμήτηρ.definition: in Od.23.97 my mother yet no mother, cf. Lyc.1174, Nonn.D.46.194

δυσμηχανέω.definition: to be at loss how to do, c. inf., A.Ag.1360

δυσμίμητος.definition: hard to imitate, D.S.1.61, Luc.Alex.20, CIG3187 ; Plu.Cat.Mi.8: Sup., Anon. Oxy. 1012ii34

δυσμνημόνευτος.definition: hard to remember; Act., remembering ill, unmindful, Pl.Ti.74e

δύσμορος.definition: ill-fated, Il.22.60, etc.; S.OC1109, cf. Men.Sam.40, Lyc.897, Opp.C.3.217: in Prose, Antipho3.2.11. Adv. with ill fortune, prob. in A.Th.837

δυσμόχλευτος.definition: hard to dislodge, Aët.3.34, Simp.in Cat.236.27

δυσνίκητος.definition: hard to conquer, J.AJ18.1.6, cf. Plu.Comp.Pel.Marc.2, D.C.43.28

δυσνοέω.definition: to be ill-affected, LXX3 Ma.3.24, Plu.Cic.38

δύσνοος.definition: contr. ill-affected, disaffected, S.Ant.212; Th.2.60; X.HG2.1.2: abs., E.IT350, Plu.2.176b. Adv. Poll.2.230

δυσξήραντος.definition: hard to dry, Thphr.CP1.4.3, Plu.2.627d, etc

δυσξύμβολος.definition: hard to deal with, driving a hard; = foreg., Poll.5.150

δυσξύνετος.definition: hard to understand, E.Ph.1506 ; X.Mem.4.7.3; Plu.2.975f , Iamb.VP35.252

δυσοδία.definition: badness of roads, App.Syr.21: pl., in concrete sense, Ptol.Tetr.197: metaph., difficulty, Plu.2.448a, cf. Ph.2.67; Demetr.Lac.1012.50 F.; Sor.2.20

δυσοδοπαίπαλος.definition: difficult and rugged, prop. of a mountain road: metaph., A.Eu.387

δύσοδος.definition: hard to pass, scarce passable, Th.1.107, Poll.3.96

δυσοίκητος.definition: bad to dwell in, Hp.Aër.19, X.Cyr.8.6.21

δυσοικονόμητος.definition: hard to digest, Diph.Siph. ap; difficult to manage, Artem.2.58

δύσοιμος.definition: acc. to Sch. and Hsch., = A.Ch.945 ; or perh. , a sad theme, cf. Hsch

δύσοιστος.definition: hard to bear, insufferable, Hp.Mul.2.181; A.Pr.690 , Ch.745, S.Ph.508 ; Id.OC1688 ; Str.12.3.40; Jul.Gal.161b

δυσοιωνέω.definition: augurill of a thing, Phryn.PSp.62 B

δυσομίλητος.definition: hard to live with, Hierocl.p.59 A.; D.Chr.40.27

δυσόρατος.definition: hard to see, X.Cyr.1.6.40, Ph.1.570; ill to look on, horrible, App.Hisp.97

δύσοργος.definition: quick to anger, S.Aj.1017, Ph.377, Tr.1118

δυσοσμία.definition: an ill smell, S.Ph.876, Fr.538, Luc.Tox.29; Man.4.270

δυσουρέω.definition: to have difficulty in micturition, Diocl.Fr.141, Ruf. ap. Orib.8.24.6, Dsc.1.6, POxy.468.1, Aret.SD2.4:—Med., Hp.Vict.2.54

δυσουρία.definition: Ion. difficult micturition, Hp.Aph.3.31 , Arist.Fr.486; Plu.2.733c

δυσπαθέω.definition: suffer a hard fate, Mosch.4.84; of sickness; to be impatient, Plu.Aem.36, Per.33; Id.2.77e

δυσπαίπαλος.definition: rough and steep, Archil.115; B.5.26; Nic.Th.145; rough, Opp.H.2.369, cf. C.2.381, al

δυσπαράδεκτος.definition: hard to admit or believe; Act., hardly admitting, Sor.2.62. Adv., metaph., to be sceptical, Plb.12.4.7

δυσπαρακόμιστος.definition: hard to carry along, Plu.Demetr.19; a difficult voyage, Plb.3.61.2

δυσπαραμύθητος.definition: hard to appease, Pl.Ti.69d; admitting no consolation, J.AJ2.9.2, Poll.3.101

δυσπαράπειστος.definition: hard to dissuade, prob. in Arist.Phgn.809a35

δυσπαραποίητος.definition: hard to alter or forge, Gal.14.52, Ammon.Diff.74

δυσπαράτρεπτος.definition: hard to seduce or bribe, Poll.8.10

δυσπαροξύνομαι.definition: Pass., have a severe attack, of fever, Alex.Trall.Febr.2

δύσπαυστος.definition: hard to stop or appease, Gal.1.334

δυσπέμφελος.definition: rough and stormy, Il.16.748: as a general epith. of the sea, Hes.Th.440; stormy passage, Id.Op.618; Nonn.D.2.550: metaph., rude, uncourteous, Hes.Op.722; of a wife, Max.88

δύσπεπτος.definition: hard to digest, Arist.GA776a12, al; unripe, v.l. ap.Sch. in Nic.Al.297

δυσπέρατος.definition: hard to pass or cross, Str.4.6.6, cf.15.1.26 : metaph., E.Med.646

δυσπεριαίρετος.definition: hard to strip off, peel, prob. in Thphr.HP5.1.1

δυσπερικάθαρτος.definition: hard to peel, clean off, Thphr.HP5.1.1 codd

δυσπερίκτητος.definition: not successful in acquiring property, Paul. Al.N.3

δυσπερίληπτος.definition: hard to encompass, Posidon.6; hard to embrace in one view, treat synoptically, D.S.1.3

δυσπερίτρεπτος.definition: hard to overturn, Gal.UP3.9. Adv. Id.18.591

δυσπετής.definition: falling out ill, most difficult, S.Aj.1046. Adv. Ion. Hdt.3.107; Hp.Prog.15, A.Pr.752: Comp. Hp.Morb.1.22

δυσπεψία.definition: indigestion, Macho ap.Ath.8.341b, Ph.2.352, Dsc.5.45, Gal.7.66

δυσπήμαντος.definition: full of grievous evil, disastrous, A.Eu.481

δυσπλήρωτος.definition: hard to fill or fulfil, Poll.9.21

δυσπλοΐα.definition: Ion. difficulty of sailing, AP7.630 , Str.1.2.31: pl., Ph.1.601:—written Cat.Cod.Astr.2.178

δύσπνοια.definition: difficulty of breathing, shortness of; contrary winds, Sch.A.R.4.1

δυσπολέμητος.definition: hard to war with, A.Supp.648 , Isoc.4.138; . . D.4.4; offriendship, Luc.Tox.36

δυσπόλεμος.definition: unlucky in war, A.Pers.1013; = foreg., IG11.1105 , LXX2 Ma.12.21

δυσπολιόρκητος.definition: hard to take by siege, X.HG4.8.5 , Plb.5.3.4, J.AJ2.10.2; Corn.ND20

δυσπόνητος.definition: bringing toil and trouble, A.Pers.515; laborious, S.OC1614

δυσπόρευτος.definition: hard to pass, X.An.1.5.7; Ph.2.14; D.C.53.22

δύσποτμος.definition: unlucky, ill-starred, of persons and things, of Prometheus, A.Pr.119; of Io, Id.Supp.306; i.e. curses, Id.Th.820; S.OT888 ; E.Ba.1144, cf. Ar.Ach.419; D.H.1.17: Comp. E.Ph.1348: Sup. Plu.Comp.Per.Fab.1. Adv. A.Pers.27…

δυσπραγέω.definition: to be unlucky, A.Ag.790 , Plu.Ant.63, Al.Jb. 5.24

δυσπραξία.definition: ill success, ill luck, A.Pr.966, S.OC1399, And.2.5, Men.707: pl., A.Eu.769, S.Aj.759, Isoc.6.102

δύσπρατος.definition: hard to sell: name of a play by Antiphanes, Ath.6.262c

δυσπρόσδεκτος.definition: hardly admitted, disagreeable; Act., disinclined to entertain, M.Ant.1.5

δυσπροσήγορος.definition: hard to speak with, repulsive, D.C.Fr.11.6, Poll.1.42. Adv. Id.5.139

δυσπρόσιτος.definition: difficult of access or attack, D.H.4.54, cf. D.S.15.42, Onos.11.6; J.BJ4.10.5; D.C.40.34; of a man, E.IA345

δυσπρόσοδος.definition: difficult of access, Th.5.65; of men, unsocial, Th.1.130, cf. X.Ages.9.2, Luc.Scyth.6, Plu.Demetr.42, D.C.Fr.11.6

δυσπρόσοπτος.definition: hard to look on, horrid to behold, ib.286; Id.El.460; Plu.Aem.12. Adv. Agatharch.26

δυσπροσόρμιστος.definition: hard to land on, having few ports, Plb.1.37.4; a difficult landing, D.S.1.31

δυσπροσπέλαστος.definition: hard to get at, Plu.Pomp.28; gloss on Sch.Od.15.234

δυσπρόσπτωτος.definition: hard to apply, of stiff ointment, Gal.11.134

δυσπρόσρητος.definition: hard to speak with, condemned by Poll.5.138

δυσπρόσωπος.definition: of ill aspect, sour looks, Artem.3.47, f.l. in Plu.Mar.15, cf. Men.Rh.p.416 S

δυσραχῖτις.definition: name of a plaster, Crito ap.Gal.13.797

δύσρηκτος.definition: hard to break through, Gal.UP15.5, D.C.62.8

δύσριγος.definition: impatient of cold, sensitive to cold, Hdt.5.10, cf.Arist.HA605a20 , Men.1007, J.AJ7.14.3, Plu.2.916a; of plants, Thphr.HP6.7.3. Adv. Ruf. ap. Orib.8.24.61, Agathin.ib.10.7.17: Comp. Arist.Pr.863a2

δυσσάρκωτος.definition: healing with difficulty, of ulcers, Id.12.188, Aët.2.187

δυσσέβεια.definition: impiety, ungodliness, it verged on impiety, A.Ch.704; S.Ant.301; a charge of impiety, ib.924.—In Lyrics also A.Eu.533; Nonn.D.20.404

δυσσεβέω.definition: to be ungodly, S.Tr.1245; A.Eu.910, E.Med.755

δυσσέβημα.definition: impious act, LXX2 Ma.12.3, D.H.7.44, Scymn.684, etc

δυσσεβής.definition: ungodly, impious, profane, of persons, A.Th.598 , and their acts, S.Ant.514; Id.OC1190; E.IT694. Adv. Id.Fr.825.—This family of words is chiefly found in Trag. ); etc., are freq. also in Prose

δύσσηπτος.definition: not easily rotting, Plu.2.725b; Id.in Hes.7, cf. Gal.10.942, al

δυσσυναίσθητος.definition: hard to grasp as a whole, of an argument, Simp.in Ph.1272.13

δυσσυνάλλακτος.definition: hard to deal with, Vett. Val.115.9

δυσσυνείδητος.definition: with a bad conscience, Id.37.29, al

δυσσύνοπτος.definition: hard to get a view of, Plb.3.84.2, etc.: metaph., Iamb.VP30.182

δυστέκμαρτος.definition: hard to make out from signs, hard to trace, S.OT109; of the art of interpreting auspices, A.Pr.497; E.Hel.712; D.H.4.29; Plu.Cat. Mi.72; Ph.1.467; hard to estimate, Aret.CA1.4

δυστιθάσευτος.definition: hard to tame, Str.15.1.42, Plu.2.529b; Artem.3.12

δυστλήμων.definition: gen. suffering hard things, h. Ap.532, Orph.Fr.49vi95

δύστλητος.definition: hard to bear, Emp.116, A.Ag.1571 ; IG14.2123

δυστόκεια.definition: one who has borne a child to misery, dub. in Hsch

δυστοκέω.definition: suffer in childbirth, Hp.Aph.5.35, Pl.Tht.149d, Arist.HA587a4: metaph., Ar.Ra.1423, cf. Aristid.Or.31.11

δυστόπαστος.definition: hard to guess, E.Tr.885; Id.Supp.138, cf. Phld.Mort.37; Plu.Rom.21; Ph.1.570

δυστραπελία.definition: or difficulty of managing, D.S.4.11, 5.15; Id.17.82; unhealthiness, Iamb.VP19.92

δυστράπελος.definition: difficult to deal with; of persons, intractable, stubborn, S.Aj.914 , Arist.EE1234a5. Adv. awkwardly, clumsily, X.Oec.8.16; with difficulty, Gal.14.114

δύστρητος.definition: hard to pierce or bore, of inferior pearls, Suid

δύστριπτος.definition: hard to bruise or grind, Artem.1.70, Hippiatr.1

δύστροπος.definition: ill-conditioned, surly, peevish, E.Hipp.161; D.6.30, Ph.1.621; Plu.2.361b. Adv. Philostr.VS1.19.2

δύστρωτος.definition: hard to injure, Plu.2.983d, cf. Apollod.Poliorc.139.8: Comp., Gal.UP1.2

δυστυχέω.definition: Ion. impf. Hdt.8.105: aor. Pl.Mx.243a: pf. Id.La.183c, Isoc.4.55, Lyc.Trag.5:— Pass., v. infr.:—to be unlucky, unfortunate, Hdt. l.c., etc.; . . A.Th.482 , cf.S.Ant.1159; E.Ph.424; Id.Andr.713; Ar.Ra.1449; Pl.La.183c;…

δυστύχημα.definition: piece of ill luck, failure, misfortune, And.2.9, Lys.24.3 , Pl.Cra.395d , Onos.36.4 ; esp. of defeat in war, X.HG4.5.18, etc

δυσυπονόητος.definition: hard to detect the nature of, of a person, Ph.2.268; ib.201

δυσυπόστατος.definition: hard to withstand, D.S.17.11; of a person, Plu.Cor.8

δύσφευκτος.definition: hard to be avoided, Men.Georg.12, cf. Ph.2.268

δυσφημέω.definition: use ill words, esp. words of ill omen; trans., speak ill of, S.El.1183, E.Heracl.600, Hec.181 , Phld.Rh.1.215 S., Them.Or.13.178a:—Pass., Phld.Mort.36

δύσφημος.definition: Dor. of ill omen, boding; slanderous, shameful, Thgn.307; Men.715; abusive, Plu.Luc.18. Adv. Phryn.PSp.62 B

δύσφθαρτος.definition: hard to destroy, S.E.M.9.19; not easily spoilt, Diph.Siph. ap. Ath.3.121c, Hices.ib.87d, Xenocr.73 , Dsc.2.9

δυσφορέω.definition: impf. X.Cyr.2.2.8:—to be impatient, angry, vexed, Hdt.5.19, A.Supp.513, S.El.255, Pherecr.22 D., Ar.Th.73, Men 543.7, etc.; E.Andr.1234; A.Th.780 , J.AJ1.10.4, Hdn.3.9.7; to feel ill on getting up, Hp. l. c.; D.S.4.61…

δυσφόρητος.definition: hard to be borne, Hsch.; f. l. for E.Cyc.344

δύσφορος.definition: hard to bear, heavy; mostly of sufferings, hard to bear, grievous, Pi.N.1.55, Fr.248; A.Eu.372 , Ag.859, etc.; false, blinding fancies, S.Aj.51; our troubles, sorrows, Id.OT87, cf. El.144 ; X.Cyr.1.6.17. Adv. Hp.Epid.…

δυσφροσύνη.definition: anxiety, care, Hes.Th.528, Simon.86 : pl., E.Tr.597 , Ph.2.75

δυσφύλακτος.definition: hard to keep off or prevent, E.Ph.924, cf. Andr.728; hard to guard against or avoid, Str.11.4.2; Longin.3.3

δυσφωνία.definition: roughness of sound, Demetr.Eloc.48, Poll.2.112, Cat.Cod.Astr.2.167

δυσχείμερος.definition: wintry or stormy, Hom; bearing winter ill, Arist.HA596b5, Gp.19.2.8

δυσχείρωτος.definition: hard to subdue, , D.61.37, Plu.Alc.4, D.C.53.25 : Sup. is prob. f. l. in D.S.5.34

δυσχεραίνω.definition: impf. Pl.Tht.169d: aor; mostly intr., feel dislike, disgust or annoyance, to be displeased, And.3.35; at a thing, D.55.11; Isoc.1.26; D.H.Th.34, Plu.Pyrrh.21; Luc.Nav.10; also to have misgivings, Arist.Metaph.984a29:—…

δυσχέρασμα.definition: in pl., harsh judgements, Pl.Phlb.44d; inconveniences, Dam.Isid.66:—condemned by Poll.3.133

δυσχέρεια.definition: of things, annoyance, disgust caused by a thing, S.Ph.473, 900, cf. Pl.Plt.286b; unpleasantness, of food, D.C.68.31: pl., Plu.2.654b

δυσχερής.definition: hard to take in hand or manage; difficult, Pl.Hp.Mi.369b , etc.; Lys.24.6 ; D.60.24; difficulties, Id.10.58, al.; difficult times, Inscr.Prien.37.132

δυσχρηστέω.definition: to be intractable, Plb.27.7.10; to be in difficulties or distress, Id.4.60.8; Id.16.4.10; Id.1.51.6; ib.75.7:—also in Med., ib.87.7; Id.1.18.7, 3.11.4; of things, to be useless, Id.16.3.5:— Pass., to be brought into d…

δύσχρηστος.definition: hard to use, inconvenient, opp. Hp.Aph.2.54, cf. Sch.Il.Oxy.221 vii 14; . . X.Cyr.3.3.26; intractable, Id.Cyn.3.11; of troops, Plb.4.11.8 ; hard to use well, Isoc.8.103; inconveniences, Cic. Att.7.5.3, cf. D.S.4.8. Ad…

δύσχροια.definition: bad colour, Dsc.Ther.6, Gal.17.215, Asp.in EN44.6

δυσχωρία.definition: rough ground, X.Cyr.1.6.35; want of room, Ph.2.563, Ath.4.129c

δυσωδία.definition: foul smell, Arist.Pol.1311b34, HA626b20, Ph.2.96, Plu.2.90b, Phld. Herc.19.27, etc

δυσώνυμος.definition: bearing an ill name, hateful, Il.6.255; Od.19.571; Il.12.116; S.OC528 ; E.Fr.403; A.R.2.258; esp. bearing a name of ill omen, such as S.Aj.914 : Comp., Ph.1.680:—in S.Fr.88.9 perh. whose tongue earned him an ill name

δυσωπέω.definition: aor. Luc.Asin.38: :—put out of; in early writers only Pass., impf. Pl.Phdr.242c:—to be put out of countenance, abs., Id.Plt.285b, etc.; Id.Lg.933a; . . Id.Phdr. l.c.; Plb.20.12.6; Ph.1.639; . . Id.2.423; Phld.Rh.1.297…

δυωδεκάδρομος.definition: running the course twelve times, Pi.O.2.50

δωδεκαακτιονίκης.definition: twelve times victorious in the Actian games, BGU1074.23

δωδεκάγναμπτος.definition: bent twelve times, the post that has been doubled twelve times, Pi.O.3.33

δωδεκαδάκτυλος.definition: twelve fingers long or broad, Apollod.Poliorc.178.3; of twelve digits, of the apparent diameter of sun and moon, Cleom.2.3; the duodenum, Herophil. ap.Gal.2.572, Ruf.Anat.42

δωδεκάδραχμος.definition: sold at twelve drachmae; privileged to pay as poll-tax only twelve dr., POxy.258.8 , al

δωδεκάεδρος.definition: with twelve surfaces: dodecahedron, Euc.11 Def. 28, 13.17, Arist.Cael.307a16

δωδεκαετηρίς.definition: cycle of twelve years, Gp.1.12 tit.: pl., title of Orphic work, Suid

δωδεκάθεος.definition: of twelve Gods, cena, Suet.Aug.70; Subst. temple of the twelve Gods, Inscr.Cos43

δωδεκάμηνος.definition: of twelve months, Pi.N.11.10 : year, Thd.Da.4.26, POxy.506.15 :—poet. twelve months old, Hes.Op.752

δωδεκαμήχανος.definition: knowing twelve arts or tricks, E.Fr.755 ; of a courtesan, Ar.Ra.1327 , cf. Pl.Com.134

δωδεκάμορφος.definition: of twelve forms, Olymp.in Phd.p.199 N

δωδεκάμοχθος.definition: of twelve labours, epith. of Heracles, Lyd.Mens.4.67

δωδεκάπους.definition: gen. twelve feet long, Men.364, Gal.10.33

δωδεκάσημος.definition: of twelve times, in music, Aristid. Quint.1.14, Sch.Ar.Nu.456 cod. Ven

δωδεκάσκυτος.definition: of twelve strips of leather, Pl.Phd.110b, Plu.2.1003d

δωδεκαστάδιος.definition: twelve stades long, etc., Posidon.18 J., Str.13.1.36

δωδεκαστάσιος.definition: weighing twelve times as much, Pl.Hipparch.231d

Δωδεκάσχοινος.definition: name of a district in Egypt, OGI210.5, 670.5, Ptol.Geog.4.5.74

δωδεκάτροπος.definition: fixed circle of twelve divisions through which the zodiac is supposed to revolve, Vett. Val.179.33, Cat.Cod.Astr.5 .89, al

δωδεκέτης.definition: or twelve years old, Call.Epigr.21 , Plu.Aem.35:—in form IG4.51 , Annuario 4/5.467 :—fem. AP11.70

δωμάτιον.definition: chamber, bedchamber, Ar.Lys.160, Lys.1.17, 24, Pl.R.390c, and so prob. in X.Eph.2.1, Procop.Arc.23

δωματίτης.definition: of, belonging to the house, Paus.3.14.7, IG5.497, al. ; Sch.Pi.N.5.81: fem., A.Ag.968

δωματοφθορέω.definition: ruin the house, cj. for A.Ag.948

δωμάω.definition: build, A.R.2.531, IG14.1868, AP7.142:—more freq. in Med., ib.11.400 , Coluth.287, Orph.A.570: metaph., build up, restore to life, Lyc.48:—Pass., Antyll. ap. Orib.9.13.6; of a statue, to be set up, App.Anth.2.534

δωρεαῖος.definition: held by royal grant, Sammelb.1178a, 1178b, cf. 3937,3938 ; v. foreg. II

δωρέω.definition: fut. Hom.Fr.17: aor. Hes.Op.82; more freq. Med. . . Il.10.557; present a thing to one, Hdt.2.126, 5.37, A.Pr.253, X.An.7.3.20, etc.; Id.HG6.3.6; also present one with a thing, Hdt.1.54, 3.130, A.Pr.778; to make him pr…

δώρημα.definition: gift, present, Hdt.7.38, etc.: c. dat. pers., A.Pers.523, Eu.402, S.Tr.668: pl., E.Or.123, etc.—Rare in Prose, X.Hier.8.4, Arist.EN1099b11, and later, Ph.2.9, Ep.Jac.1.17

Δωριάζω.definition: dress like a Dorian girl, i.e. in a single; = Anacreont.10.6, Philostr.VS1.24.2

Δωριαρχέω.definition: to be archon of the Dorians, SIG668.12 , 770B2

Δωριεύς.definition: Dorian, descendant of Dorus son of

Δωρίζω.definition: Dor. imitate the Dorians in life, dialect, etc., speak Doric Greek, Theoc.15.93, Str.8.1.2, Plu.2.421b:—Pass., to be written in the Doric dialect, A.D.Synt.279.25

Δώριος.definition: also Pratin.Lyr.1.17, Arist.Pol.1276b9: —Dorian, Pi.O.3.5; Plu.Lys.5, etc.; esp. of the Dorian mode in music, Arist.Pol. l.c., 1290a22

Δωρισμός.definition: speaking in the Doric dialect, Demetr.Eloc.177

δωρόδειπνος.definition: giving dinner, i.e. a waiter, Ath.15.701b

δωροδοκέω.definition: accept as a present, esp. take as a bribe; c. acc. pers. is interpol. in D.9.45), corrupt by bribes, D.S.13.64, Arr.Epict.4.1.148, Luc.Pisc.9, etc

δωροδόκημα.definition: acceptance of a bribe; bribe, Pl.Com.119

δωροδοκία.definition: taking of bribes, freq. in Oratt., as And.4.30; Lys.21.21; Aeschin.2.3: pl., ibid.; also, giving of bribes, corruption, in pl., D.C.39.55, 50.7

δωροδόκος.definition: taking presents or bribes, corrupt; Act., bribing, Sch.Pl.Alc.2.149a, cf. AB242

δωροδοχεῖον.definition: receptacle for offerings, alms-box, Zonar. s.v

δωροξενίας γραφή.definition: indictment of a for bribing the judges to declare him an Athenian, Lys.Fr.196 S., Hyp.Fr.20, Arist.Ath.59.3

δωροφορία.definition: bringing of presents, v.l. in Ep.Rom.15.31, Alciphr.1.6 , Poll.4.47

δωροφόρος.definition: bringing presents, Pi.P.5.86, f.l. in Epigr. ap. Ath.5.209e ; tributary, Euph.78

δαίτηθεν.definition: Adv. from a feast, Od.10.216, Theoc.17.28

δαιτρευτῶς.definition: Adv. by dividing or distributing, Zonar

δεδιότως.definition: Adv. of part. pf. in fear, D.C.42.17, Vett.Val.238.32, prob. in D.H.11.47

δεδοικότως.definition: Adv. part. pf. of = Ruf.Interrog.2, Philostr.VA4.20

δεόντως.definition: Adv. of as it ought, Pl.Clit.409c, Epicur.Ep.2p.36U., SIG615.6 , Plb.1.12.7, al., Phld.Sign.17, 18, HeroAut.11.6, BGU613.29 , etc.; Plb.9.7.3; suitably, Orib.Eup.2.1, al

δεῦτε.definition: Adv., as pl. of come hither! in Hom. with pl. imper. , either expressed, Il.7.350, al.; or understood, 13.481; . . Od.8.30: rarely in Lyr., Sapph.60,65, and Trag., E.Med.894: in later Prose, LXXGe.11.4; Ev.Matt.28.6; …

δῆθεν.definition: more freq. ironically, forsooth, . . . as he pretended, Hdt.1.59; S.Tr.382; Th.1.92, cf. 127, 3.111: freq. after mostly with a word interposed, Hdt.1.73; Id.3.136, cf. 6.39, 8.5; also E.HF949; . . Id.Or.1119; Id.Ion656

δηλαδή.definition: Adv. clearly, manifestly, Epich.149, S.OT1501, E.IA1366, Timocl.3 D., etc.: ironically, on this pretext forsooth, Hdt.4.135: freq. in answers, yes plainly, of course, Ar.V.441: but better written divisim in such phras…

δήπουθεν.definition: indef. Adv. = chiefly used before a vowel , freq. in Com., Ar.V.296, Pl.140, etc.; in answer to a rhetorical question, . . Lys.6.36, cf. D.27.59, Pl.Phlb.62e, etc

διαλελυμένως.definition: Adv., laxly, Arist.Pr.900a24; not in composition, Ath.15.676f; e.g. as compared with Eust.64.22

διαμπάξ.definition: Adv. right through, through and through, c. gen., A.Pr.65, cf. Supp.945, E.Ba.994 ; A.Supp.548 ; X.HG7.4.23; Luc.DMort.27.4; Plu.Crass.25

διάνδιχα.definition: Adv. = two ways, halt between two opinions, Il.1.189; endowed thee by halves, 9.37; in tmesi, Hes.Op.13; broke it in twain, Theoc.25.256, cf. A.R.2.1109; once in Trag., E.HF1029 ; also perh. with sails and oars, A.R.1…

διαπονητότατα.definition: Adv. Sup., most elaborately, dub. l. in Id.2.20

διαρκούντως.definition: Adv. sufficiently, dub. l. in J.AJ14.13.9

διαρρήδην.definition: Adv., expressly, explicitly, h.Merc.313, Plb.3.26.5; esp. of legal enactments or treaties, Foed. ap.And.2.14; . . Lys.1.20; Is.3.68; D.19.6; Pl.Lg.698c; ib.876c

διατεταμένως.definition: Adv., with might and main, earnestly, Arist.EN1166b28; ib.1175a8, cf. Plu.Cat.Mi.26, Iamb.Protr.19, Hierocl.in CA20p.464M

διαφερόντως.definition: Adv. pres. part. Act. of; c. gen., above all others, Id.Cri.52b; Th.8.68

διέδην.definition: Adv., throughout, to the end, Hsch

διειλημμένως.definition: Adv., distinctly, precisely, X.Oec.11.25, Ptol.Tetr.11; opp. Phld.Ir.p.83W., Rh.1.158S

διερριμμένως.definition: Adv. in a disjointed way, Plb.3.58.3

διεσμιλευμένως.definition: Adv. in polished style, Poll.6.150, Hsch

διεσπαρμένως.definition: Adv., in a disjointed manner, Aristid.Quint.1.2, v.l. for sq. in Gal.UP16.1

διεσπασμένως.definition: Adv. intermittently, Hp.Epid.1.1, 3.2; in a disjointed manner, Gal.UP16.1

διεψευσμένως.definition: Adv. falsely or mistakenly, Str.1.3.1 codd., M.Ant.2.17

διηκριβωμένως.definition: Adv., exactly, carefully, Arist.Rh.Al.1420a10, Ph.1.92, cj. in Pl.Lg.965a

διημαρτημένως.definition: Adv. erroneously, Hipparch.1.1.4, al., Alex.Aphr.in Metaph.172.5

διῃρημένως.definition: Adv., separately, M.Ant.11.6, Alex.Aphr.in Metaph.296.4, Hld.10.23

διηρθρωμένως.definition: Adv. articulately, distinctly, Gal.17.160, Alex. Aphr.in Metaph.61.3, Theol.Ar.49

διηυκρινημένως.definition: Adv., carefully, exactly, v.l. in D.S.1.93

δικογραφικῶς.definition: Adv. like a writer of forensic speeches, Id. ap. Poll.8.24

Διόθεν.definition: Adv. sent from Zeus, according to his will, Il.15.489; 24.194, cf. A.Ag.43 ; Hes.Op.765

διόλου.definition: Adv. for , altogether, Phoc.2 A, Arist.Po.1459b16, etc.; of Time, always, LXX1 Ma.6.18, AP5.157 , Lyr.Alex.Adesp.37.5, Ev.Jo.19.23, etc

δίς.definition: Adv. twice, doubly, with Nouns, twice as much, Od.9.491, cf. Th.6.57, etc.; Cratin.24; Theopomp.Com.69: more freq. with Verbs, Hdt.8.104; A.Pers.173, cf. Ag.1384; S.Aj.432; Pl.Grg.498e, cf. Phlb.60a, Emp.25; twice ove…

δισσάκις.definition: poet. Adv. twice over, Arat.968, Q.S.2.56, AP6.223

δισχιδόν.definition: Adv. of foreg., in double columns, of writing, Sch. D.T.p.191 H., al

διωρισμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass. of distinctly, separately, Arist.HA521a15, Iamb.Protr.4; definitely, Plu.2.415b

δυσαποκλίτως.definition: Adv. with difficulty in bending, Herod.Med. in Rh.Mus.58.90

δυσχεραινόντως.definition: Adv. part. pres., with disgust, v.l. in Arist.Rh.1408a17

δωδεκάκις.definition: Adv. twelve times, Ar.Pl.852, Arist.Fr.347, D.C.60.7, etc

Δωριστί.definition: Adv. in Dorian fashion; in the Dorian dialect, Call.Iamb.1.354

δωροδοκιστί.definition: Adv. in bribe-fashion, Ar.Eq.996, with a play on
